Sami people
-----------

Main article: [Sami people](./Sami_people "Sami people")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/K%C3%A5ta_i_V%C3%A4stra_%C3%85r%C3%A5dalen.JPG/250px-K%C3%A5ta_i_V%C3%A4stra_%C3%85r%C3%A5dalen.JPG)](./File:Kåta_i_Västra_Årådalen.JPG)

A Sami [goahti](./Goahti "Goahti") in [Arådalen](./Arådalen "Arådalen").

In Jämtland there are also Sami people. The Sami in Jämtland are Southern Sami people and speak [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language") (or *åarjelsaemien giele*, as it is known in Southern Sami), a [language](./Sami_language "Sami language") mutually unintelligible with the other Sami languages. The Sami in Jämtland have historically been referred to as "Lapps" and sometimes by using the vague word "Finns" (supposedly related to English "find", see [Fenni](./Fenni "Fenni")), though they prefer to call themselves Sami. There have been Sami peoples in Jämtland from pre-historic times; exactly how many, however, is disputed.[[18]](./Jämtland#cite_note-18) The northernmost part of Jämtland, [Frostviken](./Frostviken_Parish?action=edit&redlink=1 "Frostviken Parish"), is originally a Sami area, historically referred to as a *finnmark*. However, the ancestors to the Sami people who live south of this area today probably did not come to the area before the 16th century,[[19]](./Jämtland#cite_note-nationalencyklopedin-19) when large-scale [reindeer](./Reindeer "Reindeer") herding began, leading to a nomadic lifestyle among the Sami people. This also led to several conflicts in court between Sami people in Jämtland and the [land owners](./Property "Property"). At the dawn of the 20th century, the Swedish state had an official policy which stated that "Lapp should be Lapp" and that they should all live a "traditional" Sami life and not integrate in the society. This has now changed and only a minority are in fact reindeer-herders. The Sami people in Jämtland are closely connected to their brethren living in Trøndelag, and a distinctive feature of the Southern Sami culture is the [yoik](./Yoik "Yoik") called *vuoille*.

Heraldry
--------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/J%C3%A4mtland_coat_of_arms.png/250px-J%C3%A4mtland_coat_of_arms.png)](./File:Jämtland_coat_of_arms.png)

Popular belief holds that the scene represents Jämtland torn between Norway and Sweden.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)

The arms are represented with a ducal coronet. [Blazon](./Blazon "Blazon"):

:   *I blått fält en gående älg av silver med en lyftande falk på ryggen och i posten åtföljd av en vänstervänd, upprest hund, båda av guld.*[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)[[21]](./Jämtland#cite_note-SHS-21)

[English](./English_language "English language") translation:

:   "In a blue field, a walking [moose](./Moose "Moose") of silver [with red antlers] with a striking falcon on its back accompanied by a reared hound in front, both of gold."

The coat of arms of Jämtland, created for [Karl X Gustav](./Charles_X_Gustav_of_Sweden "Charles X Gustav of Sweden")'s funeral, derived from a seal which had been granted to Jämtland in 1635 by the [Danish-Norwegian king](./Christian_IV_of_Denmark "Christian IV of Denmark").[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) The beasts on this seal were difficult to identify. (Is the primary animal a deer, moose or reindeer? Is it a dog, wolf or bear? An eagle or a falcon?) The identity of these animals as a moose between a dog and a falcon was settled in 1884. According to popular perception, these represent Jämtland torn between Norway and Sweden, though obviously this meaning was not officially assigned by any royal authority.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) Svante Höglin claimed the scene to portray a moose hunted by a trained hunting dog and falcon, and in 1935 the coat of arms was revised, adding a collar and a bell to aid in identifying the dog and the falcon, respectively.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) Strangely, the revised blazon does not mention the moose's [attire](./Antler "Antler") although the prototype in the *Riksheraldikerämbetet* (Swedish National Heraldry Office) is provided with secondary colours for the antlers, beak, hooves and claws.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)

Jämtland's first seal was the one depicted above from the medieval period. It was abolished after the [Nordic Seven Years' War](./Nordic_Seven_Years'_War "Nordic Seven Years' War") and the second seal of Jämtland was used between 1575 and 1614. This seal contained two [Olav-axes](./Olav-axe?action=edit&redlink=1 "Olav-axe") and was also abolished after a Swedish occupation, the one during the [Kalmar War](./Kalmar_War "Kalmar War"). When Jämtland became Swedish it was not suitable to use one of the older seals with such a strong Norwegian influence as a basis for a new Swedish coat of arms. So the latest seal was used instead, even though it was in fact of Danish origin.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Current administration
----------------------

Just like every other historical province of Sweden Jämtland serves no administrative purposes, but serves as an historical, geographical and cultural region. Jämtland makes up three quarters of the [Swedish administrative province](./Län "Län") [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County"), though a small uninhabited part in northern Jämtland is a part of [Västerbotten County](./Västerbotten_County "Västerbotten County") and the area around [Överturingen](./Överturingen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Överturingen") is a part of [Västernorrland County](./Västernorrland_County "Västernorrland County"). The landsting, *[County Council](./County_Councils_of_Sweden "County Councils of Sweden")*, is an elected assembly and the successor of Jamtamót. This County Council was the role model for the rest of the Swedish County Councils when they were established in 1863.[[22]](./Jämtland#cite_note-22)

The province is also divided into primarily seven [municipalities](./Municipalities "Municipalities"); [Berg Municipality](./Berg_Municipality "Berg Municipality"), [Bräcke Municipality](./Bräcke_Municipality "Bräcke Municipality"), [Krokom Municipality](./Krokom_Municipality "Krokom Municipality"), [Ragunda Municipality](./Ragunda_Municipality "Ragunda Municipality"), [Strömsund Municipality](./Strömsund_Municipality "Strömsund Municipality"), [Åre Municipality](./Åre_Municipality "Åre Municipality") and [Östersund Municipality](./Östersund_Municipality "Östersund Municipality"). The uninhabited part in northern Jämtland belongs to [Dorotea Municipality](./Dorotea_Municipality "Dorotea Municipality") and the area around Överturingen is a part of [Ånge Municipality](./Ånge_Municipality "Ånge Municipality").

Though, even if these municipalities and the county are serving as administrative regions most Jamts still identify themselves with the parishes and with Jämtland as a province.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Storsj%C3%B6n_med_fj%C3%A4ll.jpg/250px-Storsj%C3%B6n_med_fj%C3%A4ll.jpg)](./File:Storsjön_med_fjäll.jpg)

The mountains in Scandinavia are referred to as *[fells](./Fell "Fell")*. This picture shows Storsjön, "the Great Lake" and distant fells.

Jämtland is a large land-locked province in the heart of the [Scandinavian Peninsula](./Scandinavian_Peninsula "Scandinavian Peninsula") in [northern Europe](./Northern_Europe "Northern Europe"). Jämtland stretches 315 kilometers in north–south direction and 250 kilometers in east–west direction and is equal in size with e.g. [Ireland](./Ireland "Ireland"). Jämtland's western border is made out by [Kölen](./Scandinavian_Mountains "Scandinavian Mountains") which stretches throughout the province from north to south with branches into the landscape's southeastern parts. The fell [massif](./Massif "Massif") is broken at some places by large valleys stretching all the way to the [Norwegian Sea](./Norwegian_Sea "Norwegian Sea"). These valleys have been used for centuries as paths connecting Jämtland to the west. The valleys were particularly heavily used during [pilgrimages](./Pilgrimage "Pilgrimage") to [Nidaros](./Nidaros "Nidaros"), the fourth most visited pilgrimage site during the medieval period. In fact no less than three pilgrim roads went through Jämtland.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/T%C3%A4nnforsen.jpg/250px-T%C3%A4nnforsen.jpg)](./File:Tännforsen.jpg)

[Tännforsen](./Tännforsen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tännforsen") in western Jämtland

The entire province is more or less a [highland region](./Highland_(geography) "Highland (geography)") with the highest peak being [Storsylen](./Storsylen "Storsylen"), a peak in the [Sylan](./Sylan "Sylan") mountain range with an [altitude](./Altitude "Altitude") of 1 728 meters above sea level. Though this is not the highest peak in the mountain range, since that peak is in fact located on the other side of the border. Another large peak in Jämtland worthy of mention is [Åreskutan](./Åreskutan "Åreskutan") (1 420 meters above sea level).
The lowest point in the province is as low as 35 meters above sea level and is located in the eastern part of Jämtland.

Approximately 8 per cent of Jämtland's area is covered by water and the province has two larger [streams](./Stream "Stream"), [Ljungan](./Ljungan "Ljungan") and [Indalsälven](./Indalsälven "Indalsälven") (also known as *Jämtlandsälven*). Both of which emanates from the Scandinavian Mountains and drains several lakes on their way eastwards to lower altitudes.

### Climate

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Jamtlandvy.jpg/250px-Jamtlandvy.jpg)](./File:Jamtlandvy.jpg)

Summer scenery in Jämtland

Jämtland has a [temperate climate](./Temperate_climate "Temperate climate") and belongs to the [temperate zone](./Temperate_zone "Temperate zone")'s northernmost area. The climate in Jämtland is both [humid continental](./Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") and [subarctic](./Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate"), depending on the location. The climate is greatly affected by the [Norwegian Sea](./Norwegian_Sea "Norwegian Sea") and the [Atlantic Ocean](./Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean"), due to several [mountain passes](./Mountain_pass "Mountain pass") in Scandinavian mountain range.

In western Jämtland mild winters with excessive [precipitation](./Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)") are common. This is because of the warm winds brought to the area by the [Gulf Stream](./Gulf_Stream "Gulf Stream"). The average precipitation in the Jamtish Fells is roughly 1 000 [millimetres](./Millimetre "Millimetre") per year, with [Skäckerfjällen](./Skäckerfjällen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skäckerfjällen") as extreme with about 1 500 mm. The precipitation rates in the middle of the province are much more moderate. In fact the central and eastern parts of Jämtland have precipitation shortages, in Storsjöbygden the annual averages is as low as 500 mm. Due to the warm winds the temperature during the winters reaches its maximum in the fell region with about -7-8[°C](./°C "°C") in [Storlien](./Storlien "Storlien") and the environs. The coldest winter temperatures are found in the province's outskirts like [Börtnan](./Börtnan?action=edit&redlink=1 "Börtnan") with roughly -11 °C.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Maximum temperatures in the summer months average from the 14 °C in Jämtland's eastern parts to around 11 °C in the fell region.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Though on certain mountain peaks the averages are usually as low as 5 °C.

The highest (34.0 °C) and lowest (-45.8 °C) temperatures ever recorded in Jämtland were found in its easternmost parts near [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand "Hammarstrand") in 1947 and 1950, respectively.

[Blizzards](./Blizzard "Blizzard") are common in Jämtland, and especially in the fell region. The most notable blizzard is the one that arose on [New Year's Eve](./New_Year's_Eve "New Year's Eve") 1718 (see above). The heaviest winds in Jämtland may gust to 55 metres/s (198 km/h, 123 mph).

Wildlife
--------

### Flora

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG/120px-Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG)](./File:Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG)

*Gymnadenia nigra*, known as *brunkulla* — the *brown maiden* in Jamtish dialect.

The Jamtish [flora](./Flora "Flora") is heavily characterized by [temperate coniferous forest](./Temperate_coniferous_forest "Temperate coniferous forest"), [taiga](./Taiga "Taiga"), a forest inhabited by [Norway spruce](./Norway_spruce "Norway spruce") and [pine](./Pine "Pine") trees. Among the two the Norway spruce is more common. The Norway spruce actually grows most densely in Jämtland together with the southern parts of [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden "Lapland, Sweden"). Here roughly 60 percent of the forests consist of spruces.

In Jämtland over 2,300 mineral-rich [marshes](./Marsh "Marsh") ([wetlands](./Wetland "Wetland")) containing a very high [pH](./PH "PH") level have been located. These marshes cover an area of 550 square kilometers. 400 of these marshes are also very rich in [chalk](./Chalk "Chalk") and because of the chalk-rich soil Jämtland displays the largest concentration of these types of marshes on the entire European continent. The chalk-rich soil has attracted several chalk-dependent plants, such as [orchids](./Orchid "Orchid"), in Jämtland there are 19 different kinds of orchids.

Each province in Sweden has symbols associated with them and Jämtland's provincial [flower](./Flower "Flower") is an extremely rare orchid, the *[Gymnadenia nigra](./Gymnadenia_nigra "Gymnadenia nigra")*, an orchid that's only common in the province and a few other places in central Scandinavia. Several kinds of [berries](./Berry "Berry") are found in Jämtland like e.g. [bilberry](./Bilberry "Bilberry") (*blåbär*), [lingonberry](./Lingonberry "Lingonberry") (*lyngbär*) and [cloudberry](./Cloudberry "Cloudberry") (referred to as *mylhta* in Jämtland).

### Fauna

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](./File:Moose_Zoo_Östersund.jpg)

A tame Jamtish moose from [Moose Garden](./Moose_Garden?action=edit&redlink=1 "Moose Garden") in [Orrviken](./Orrviken "Orrviken") outside Östersund. The moose is Jämtland's provincial animal.

Due to the diversified [natural environment](./Natural_environment "Natural environment") in Jämtland it displays a great deal of different [animals](./Animal "Animal"). The animal most commonly associated with Jämtland is (as already hinted) the [moose](./Moose "Moose"). It is Jämtland's provincial animal and is referred to in dialect as simply *djur*, "animal". Moose may be found throughout Jämtland but to a lesser extent in the mountainous area in the province's eastern parts and in the north.

However northern Jämtland is the most densely populated [brown bear](./Brown_bear "Brown bear") habitat in the world. The brown bear (*bjenn* in Jamtish) is also more or less common throughout Jämtland. Other large predators in Jämtland include the [cat](./Felidae "Felidae") *gaupa* ([Eurasian lynx](./Eurasian_lynx "Eurasian lynx")), the *filfras* meaning the glutton ([wolverine](./Wolverine "Wolverine")) and smaller such as the [Arctic fox](./Arctic_fox "Arctic fox"). Jämtland has had populations of [wolves](./Wolf "Wolf") (*skrågg*, *gråbein*) from time to time after it practically became extinct in Scandinavia during the 20th century. There are however currently no wolves with an established [territory](./Territory_(animal) "Territory (animal)") in Jämtland. There is also one large [raptor](./Bird_of_prey "Bird of prey") in the province, the [golden eagle](./Golden_eagle "Golden eagle").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Beaver_dam_J%C3%A4mtland.JPG/250px-Beaver_dam_J%C3%A4mtland.JPG)](./File:Beaver_dam_Jämtland.JPG)

A [beaver dam](./Beaver_dam "Beaver dam") in Jämtland.

The last native [beaver](./Beaver "Beaver") in Sweden was shot in northern Jämtland 1871 at [Bjurälven](./Bjurälven "Bjurälven") (*bjur* or *björ* is the Jamtish word for beaver). It was also in Jämtland that the beaver was reintroduced in Sweden from Norway in 1922. The current beaver population is quite large and common. Among the smaller mammals inhabiting Jämtland that are rare in the rest of Scandinavia are e.g. the [taiga shrew](./Taiga_shrew "Taiga shrew") and the [northern birch mouse](./Northern_birch_mouse "Northern birch mouse"). The *læmel*, [Norway lemming](./Norway_lemming "Norway lemming") is also present in Jämtland and the latest major population boom usual for this species occurred in 2001.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Albino_raindeer.jpg/250px-Albino_raindeer.jpg)](./File:Albino_raindeer.jpg)

Reindeer in Jämtland's mountain range.

Jämtland is inhabited by several mammals from the [weasel family](./Weasel_family "Weasel family"). Besides the already mentioned wolverine the *oter*, [otter](./Eurasian_otter "Eurasian otter"), is widespread in the province and common near several streams, the [least or snow weasel](./Least_weasel "Least weasel") exists, along with planted, released and escaped [minks](./Mink "Mink"). The province is also home to the [pine marten](./Pine_marten "Pine marten") and the [ermine](./Stoat "Stoat"). These mammals have often been hunted for their valuable fur, for Jämtland this is especially true for the ermine.

Among the [deer](./Deer "Deer") the moose is as already stated common. Other deer are [roe deer](./Roe_deer "Roe deer"), [red deer](./Red_deer "Red deer") and [reindeer](./Reindeer "Reindeer"), in the shape of Sami herds or wilded originally tame reindeers.

The provincial [fish](./Fish "Fish") is the [brown trout](./Brown_trout "Brown trout") which is found together with [common whitefish](./Common_whitefish "Common whitefish"), [grayling](./Thymallus_thymallus "Thymallus thymallus"), [European perch](./European_perch "European perch"), [Arctic char](./Arctic_char "Arctic char"), [burbot](./Burbot "Burbot"), [salmon](./Salmon "Salmon") and the carnivorous [northern pike](./Northern_pike "Northern pike"). Roughly 250 types of [birds](./Bird "Bird") have been observed in Jämtland. The species presence greatly varies, in the fells [bluethroat](./Bluethroat "Bluethroat"), [long-tailed skua](./Long-tailed_skua "Long-tailed skua"), [Eurasian dotterel](./Eurasian_dotterel "Eurasian dotterel"), [ptarmigan](./Rock_ptarmigan "Rock ptarmigan"), [Lapland](./Lapland_bunting "Lapland bunting") and [snow bunting](./Snow_bunting "Snow bunting") are found. The forested region is inhabited by species such as [hazel hen](./Hazel_hen "Hazel hen"), [black grouse](./Black_grouse "Black grouse"), [capercaillie](./Capercaillie "Capercaillie"), [Siberian jay](./Siberian_jay "Siberian jay"), [three-toed woodpecker](./Eurasian_three-toed_woodpecker "Eurasian three-toed woodpecker") and [rustic bunting](./Rustic_bunting "Rustic bunting"). Several different types of [owls](./Owl "Owl") dwells in the province and the provincial owl is the [northern hawk owl](./Northern_hawk_owl "Northern hawk owl").

Economy
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg/250px-Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg)](./File:Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg)

The [freeskiing](./Freeskiing "Freeskiing") competition [Jon Olsson](./Jon_Olsson "Jon Olsson") invitational in [Åre](./Åre "Åre")

The first humans came to Jämtland after the last ice age and later switched to a more agricultural lifestyle. Though the agriculture could not sustain the population so it was combined with a great deal of trading, hunting and iron production. When the rise of industrialism begun, Jämtland was one of the few Swedish regions that never became fully industrialized. Instead Jämtland supplied the Norrlandic coast with raw materials, mainly [lumber](./Lumber "Lumber"). The focus in Jämtland's [economy](./Economy "Economy") was directed towards tourism after the construction of the railroad, starting with the "clean air tourists" who came to experience the fresh air, to see the snow clad fells, the waterfalls and the natural environment. Today the tourism in Jämtland is dominated by winter sports and especially alpine skiing in various facilities in [Åre](./Åre_(ski_area) "Åre (ski area)"), [Bydalen](./Bydalen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bydalen"), [Storlien](./Storlien "Storlien"), [Klövsjö](./Klövsjö "Klövsjö"), etc.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Lill%C3%A4nge_handelsplats_070616.jpg/250px-Lill%C3%A4nge_handelsplats_070616.jpg)](./File:Lillänge_handelsplats_070616.jpg)

[Lillänge](./Lillänge?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lillänge") is an external shopping centre in Östersund

As Jämtland never industrialized the agricultural sector is larger compared to the rest of Sweden. In Jämtland County this sector employs 4,4 per cent of the labour force compared to 1,8 per cent for Sweden as whole.[[23]](./Jämtland#cite_note-23) Just like the rest of Sweden the [public sector](./Public_sector "Public sector") in Jämtland is large and the high [taxes](./Taxes "Taxes") fund the [public welfare](./Swedish_welfare "Swedish welfare").

Jämtland has large concentrations of [uranium](./Uranium "Uranium") and deposits of e.g. [gold](./Gold "Gold"), [zinc](./Zinc "Zinc"), [mica](./Mica "Mica"), [silver](./Silver "Silver"), [lead](./Lead "Lead"), [iron](./Iron "Iron") and [copper](./Copper "Copper") have been found. However, the only [mines](./Mining "Mining") of importance in Jämtland's history are the former copper mines in [Fröå](./Fröå?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fröå") and [Huså](./Huså?action=edit&redlink=1 "Huså").

Jämtland is heavily dominated by many [small businesses](./Small_business "Small business") and together with Härjedalen Jämtland has the second highest number of [company owners](./Company_owner "Company owner") in Sweden (in relation to the population), the highest number of enterprising women[[24]](./Jämtland#cite_note-24) and by far the most [cooperatives](./Cooperative "Cooperative").[[25]](./Jämtland#cite_note-25) [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund") is the centre of trade and commerce in Jämtland.

Population
----------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg/250px-20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg)](./File:20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg)

[King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building](./King_Chulalongkorn_Memorial_Building "King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building") nearby the small village [Bispgården](./Västra_Bispgården "Västra Bispgården"), easternmost Jämtland

With the exception of the city of [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund") and its surrounding areas, Jämtland is a very sparsely populated region. In Jämtland as a whole, there are only 3.4 people per square kilometre, and the population of 115,331[[1]](./Jämtland#cite_note-population-1) is unevenly distributed, with more than half its population (approximately 60 000) living in the Östersund area.

In Jämtland County (including the province of Härjedalen) the number of people living outside an urban area is 34% of the total population, making Jämtland one of the largest rural regions in Scandinavia. Most people in Jämtland live in [Storsjöbygden](./Storsjöbygden?action=edit&redlink=1 "Storsjöbygden"), the area around lake Storsjön which includes Jämtland's only [chartered city](./Cities_of_Sweden "Cities of Sweden"), [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"), founded 1786 (now including Frösön), [Krokom](./Krokom "Krokom"), [Ås](./Ås,_Krokom "Ås, Krokom"), [Svenstavik](./Svenstavik "Svenstavik"), [Nälden](./Nälden "Nälden") and Jämtland's second largest town [Brunflo](./Brunflo "Brunflo"). This region is actually quite densely populated. The largest urban areas outside Storsjöbygden are primly the municipality seats [Strömsund](./Strömsund "Strömsund"), [Järpen](./Järpen "Järpen"), [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke") and [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand "Hammarstrand"), along with towns such as [Hammerdal](./Hammerdal "Hammerdal"), Lit, and the ski resort [Åre](./Åre "Åre").

A resident or native of Jämtland is commonly referred to as *Jamt* (Swedish: *jämte*).

Culture
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg/250px-Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg)](./File:Ostra_Aradalen1_Sweden.jpg)

Traditional summer houses, *buvåll* "critter house" in Jämtland. 'Bu' is [cognate](./Cognate "Cognate") to the English word "booth" and 'våll' to "[weald](./Weald "Weald")"

[![Jämthund](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/J%C3%A4mthund_drvd.png/250px-J%C3%A4mthund_drvd.png)](./File:Jämthund_drvd.png "Jämthund")

Jämthund

The culture of Jämtland has been greatly affected by the fact that Jämtland has never had an [upper class](./Upper_class "Upper class"), since the population have mostly consisted of free sovereign farmers with wide connections and a strong regional identity.[[26]](./Jämtland#cite_note-26) This has been the case for many generations. When [Christian IV of Denmark](./Christian_IV_of_Denmark "Christian IV of Denmark") punished the Jamts severely after having sworn the Swedish king their allegiance (see above) by turning them into [tenant farmers](./Tenant_farmer "Tenant farmer") and abolished their seal, he told them to stay put on their farms. They did not heed this call but instead sought help from their own organized advisors and "the land's defense", an insolence that further outraged the Danish king. Jämtland started out free and remained autonomous during its time as a Norwegian [dependency](./Dependent_territory "Dependent territory"). Because of Jämtland's historical background the local culture shows great similarities with the [Norwegian farm culture](./Norwegian_farm_culture "Norwegian farm culture").

Today, the history of Jämtland is exhibited in the regional museum [Jamtli](./Jamtli "Jamtli") in [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"). The museum consists of an [open-air section](./Open-air_museum "Open-air museum") with historical buildings, as well as an indoor museum which houses exhibitions about the region's cultural history, from the Stone Age until modern times. Local history has been very popular in Jämtland for over 100 years, due to the extensive cultural home ground movement that emerged in the late 19th and early 20th century. The movement founded Jamtli to preserve the cultural heritage.

### Lifestyle

The culture in Jämtland has been marked by the stages in human development; the hunting-gathering stage, the semi-nomadic herding stage, the fully agricultural stage and the modern technological stage.

Remnants from the hunter-gathering stage is first and foremost hunting itself. Jämtland's population remained in this stage for a very long time due to the hunters ability to sustain the population. Today the moose hunt is regarded by many Jamts as the major holiday of the year. When the first humans came to Jämtland they brought dogs with them as helpers. The local dog, [Jämthund](./Jämthund "Jämthund"), is a canine breed eponymous to Jämtland. Even if it is not explicitly stated, popular perception holds that the dog depicted in the coat of arms is of that breed. The Jämthund is often described having a [wolf](./Wolf "Wolf")-like appearance.

One of the first things [Tacitus](./Tacitus "Tacitus") mentions in his work *[Germania](./Germania_(book) "Germania (book)")* is that the Germanic people treasure their animals above all else. Tacitus also concludes that the Germanic people found cultivation repulsive. Instead, he states, the Germanic people devote themselves to food and sleep and besides that they prefer to remain idle. All of this, to certain extents, applied to Jämtland. When the people of Jämtland settled down they relied mostly on [pastoralism](./Pastoralism "Pastoralism") ([transhumance](./Transhumance "Transhumance")). Their animals were the source of wealth and they were therefore loved by their owners. This love for the [livestock](./Livestock "Livestock") has manifested itself in the dialect, a male [nipple](./Nipple "Nipple") is called *bokkjen* (the [buck](./Goat#Etymology "Goat")) and a female nipple is known as *geita* (the [goat](./Goat "Goat")).

In Jämtland the Scandinavian inland transhumance, *buföring*, has always been more important than cultivation. In fact it was crucial to take care of the livestock and supply them with food, and rewarding. Every summer for several weeks, from May to September, *gjetaran* (herd boys) and *butøusan* (herd girls, *bu* is cognate to "booth") followed and guarded *kreka*, the critter, on their way to a [grazing land](./Grazing "Grazing") on higher altitudes where several critter houses had been raised. The common animals taken out on these journeys were *gjettran* (Jämtland goats) and *kynnan* (the fell cows) a white, brisk and headstrong cow race, lacking horns. It was a hard work and it depended on cooperation between males and females. This lifestyle lived on for thousand years and it was first in the 1950s it became obsolete. This tradition has however been resurrected as of late, mostly for touristic purposes.

When the population settled down the society greatly changed, first coexisting with the older societies, later absorbing them. Trade became much more important, a political institution elected by the people came into existence, the very same institution whose successor is the current County Council. Jämtland got its name and a somewhat [hierarchical](./Hierarchy "Hierarchy") social structure emerged, though, as already pointed out, Jämtland never had an upper class. Strong families such as [Skanke](./Skanke "Skanke") and [Blix](./Blix_(noble_family)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Blix (noble family)") did exist though and on the countryside in Jämtland people still live in networks of relatives, *families*. Where they provide a second [social security](./Social_security "Social security") for many, in the rest of Sweden and in e.g. Östersund this has completely or almost entirely been replaced by [public welfare](./Public_welfare "Public welfare").

### Cuisine

See also: [Cuisine of Norway](./Cuisine_of_Norway "Cuisine of Norway") and [Cuisine of Sweden](./Cuisine_of_Sweden "Cuisine of Sweden")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Messmor.jpg/250px-Messmor.jpg)](./File:Messmor.jpg)

*Messmör*, soft whey butter, is a Jamtish product popular in Sweden

Much of Jämtland's cuisine is remnant from the herding stage. Just like other Scandinavians, it is common among Jamts to drink [milk](./Milk "Milk") throughout their entire life. There are many different types of Jamtish [dairy products](./Dairy_products "Dairy products"), especially cheese, since it was by far the easiest way to conserve milk. [Mesost](./Brunost "Brunost") is particularly associated with Jämtland and also e.g. a local variant of [cottage cheese](./Cottage_cheese "Cottage cheese") called *grynost*. In Jämtland there are several small [dairies](./Dairy "Dairy") in the villages, most famous is the one in [Skärvången](./Skärvången?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skärvången"). Other products associated with Jämtland are the [soft whey butter](./Soft_whey_butter?action=edit&redlink=1 "Soft whey butter"), [long fil](./Long_fil?action=edit&redlink=1 "Long fil"), [kjesfil](./Kjesfil?action=edit&redlink=1 "Kjesfil"), *flautgröt* "[cream](./Cream "Cream") [porridge](./Porridge "Porridge")", [tunnbröd](./Tunnbröd "Tunnbröd"), a version of [palt](./Palt "Palt") called *kams*, klobb etc.

The ancient practice of brewing *Julöl* (yule beer) persists even today with the [microbrewery](./Microbrewery "Microbrewery") [Jämtlands Bryggeri](./Jämtlands_Bryggeri "Jämtlands Bryggeri") in [Pilgrimstad](./Pilgrimstad "Pilgrimstad").

Local projects such as the internet portal [Food of Jämtland](http://www.foodofjamtland.se/english) and the trading mark *[Smakriket Jämtland](https://www.smakriket.se)* (the "taste realm" Jämtland) are two major contributors in marketing, preserving and developing the cuisine of Jämtland.

Some of the newest merchandises in Jämtland are a [sparkling wine](./Sparkling_wine "Sparkling wine") made of [birch](./Birch "Birch") [sap](./Sap "Sap") and a [sausage](./Sausage "Sausage") called *Jämtlandsfalu*, wilderness juice, the [snaps](./Snaps "Snaps") *kallsup* and tunnbröd [chips.](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/chips "wikt:chips")

### Folklore

See also: [Scandinavian folklore](./Scandinavian_folklore "Scandinavian folklore")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/PB190187.JPG/250px-PB190187.JPG)](./File:PB190187.JPG)

Lake Storsjön

The folklore of Jämtland mostly correspond to [Scandinavian folklore](./Scandinavian_folklore "Scandinavian folklore") as whole, although the folklore is seldom regarded as popular belief nowadays, with one major exception, [Storsjöodjuret](./Storsjöodjuret "Storsjöodjuret").

According to legend it is believed that [Storsjön](./Storsjön "Storsjön") (literally *the Great Lake*) harbors a large lake creature, Storsjöodjuret. There are many witness reports but the creature's existence remains to be established conclusively. Regardless of any proven existence, Storsjöodjuret was officially placed under the protection of a degree issued in 1986 by the [County Administrative Board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden") to guarantee its safety from hunters and fortune seekers, the protection was lifted in November 2005.[[27]](./Jämtland#cite_note-27) The first description of Storsjöodjuret was made in this tale from 1635;

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg/250px-Draak_%C3%96stersund_22jul2006.jpg)](./File:Draak_Östersund_22jul2006.jpg)

Storsjöodjuret is commonly represented by this figure.


> A long, long time ago two trolls, Jata and Kata, stood on the shores of the Great Lake brewing a concoction in their cauldrons. They brewed and mixed and added to the liquid for days and weeks and years. They knew not what would result from their brew but they wondered about it a great deal. One evening there was heard a strange sound from one of their cauldrons. There was a wailing, a groaning and a crying, then suddenly came a loud bang. A strange animal with a black serpentine body and a cat-like head jumped out of the cauldron and disappeared into the lake. The monster enjoyed living in the lake, grew unbelievably larger and awakened terror among the people whenever it appeared. Finally, it extended all the way round the island of Frösön, and could even bite its own tail. Ketil Runske bound the mighty monster with a strong spell which was carved on a stone and raised on the island of Frösön. The serpent was pictured on the stone. Thus was the spell to be tied till the day someone came who could read and understand the inscription on the stone.

*[Puken](./Puken?action=edit&redlink=1 "Puken")* is a magical ball of [yarn](./Yarn "Yarn") summoned by a witch to draw objects to her. It often steals milk to the witch by milking [cows](./Cow "Cow").[[28]](./Jämtland#cite_note-28)

Just like in the rest of the world [dragons](./Dragon "Dragon") have been known for a long time. In Jämtland they resemble [brooms](./Broom "Broom"), that flies quickly and strikes down where [treasuries](./Treasury "Treasury") are buried.[[29]](./Jämtland#cite_note-29)

*[Sjörå](./Sjörå "Sjörå")* is a keeper of freshwater, that master fish, [aas](./River "River") and lakes. It is similar to the Jamtish *[skogskjæringa](./Hulder "Hulder")* "wife of the forest". A being that, at day, takes the appearance of a *[rauvtjuksa](./Siberian_jay "Siberian jay")* "red tail", a bird seen as ominous in Jamtish folklore. When in physical form her tail is always apparent. She tries to lure men to have [sexual intercourse](./Sexual_intercourse "Sexual intercourse") with her. The *skogsrå* is not the same creature as skogskjæringa in Jamtish folklore, it is the keeper of the forest and master all the animals in it. It takes on the shape of a moose during hunting season, and grows larger and larger if hit by bullets and eventually forces the hunters out. It can however, be slain with a silver bullet.[[30]](./Jämtland#cite_note-30)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg/250px-Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg)](./File:Johan_Tirens_naecken.jpg)

Local artist [Johan Tirén](./Johan_Tirén "Johan Tirén")'s painting *Jämtlandssägen* (Jämtland's tale) with a young fiddler wearing traditional Great Jamtish clothes, whilst listening to the Nix play.

[Tomten](./Tomte "Tomte") is a common creature, it is quite tall and has an eye in the middle of his forehead. It is the keeper of [barns](./Barn "Barn") and a very capricious being, though he usually brings luck.[[31]](./Jämtland#cite_note-p_98-31)

The [Nix](./Neck_(water_spirit) "Neck (water spirit)"), *Näkkjen*, is a common mythical creature, in Jämtland it refers to a male water spirit whose music was dangerous to women. Each year in the town of [Hackås](./Hackås "Hackås") in southern Jämtland an annual [traditional music](./Traditional_Nordic_dance_music "Traditional Nordic dance music") contest *[Årets Näck](./Årets_Näck "Årets Näck")* is held where each contestant impersonates the Nix.

In Jämtland the [vættir](./Vættir "Vættir")/[dwarves](./Dwarf_(mythology) "Dwarf (mythology)") goes by the name *jolbyggar* "earth builders". They herd large white goats and cows and live underground, they are considered innocuous though sometimes they exchange an unbaptized child for a so-called *bytningsbarn*. They are commonly associated with the grazing lands.[[31]](./Jämtland#cite_note-p_98-31) They also go by the names *småruskan*, *smågubban* and *småtussan*.

### Folk costumes

Jämtland has several different types of folk costumes or *[bunads](./Bunad "Bunad")*. Unlike certain regions in Scandinavia a unitary bunad did not exist in Jämtland's parishes, with the exception of [Hammerdal parish](./Hammerdal_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hammerdal parish") with its [brown](./Brown "Brown")-striped clothing.

Usually Jämtland is divided into three different clothing parts, the North Jamtish ([Hammerdal](./Hammerdal_Court_District "Hammerdal Court District")), the East Jamtish ([Ragunda](./Ragunda_Court_District "Ragunda Court District")) and the Great Jamtish area, covering the rest and the majority of Jämtland.

The North Jamtish clothing part is typically influenced by the folk costumes of northern Ångermanland and to a lesser degree Lapland, with the exception of [Frostviken parish](./Frostviken_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 "Frostviken parish") settled by [Trønders](./Trøndersk "Trøndersk") in the 18th century. The East Jamtish part is the least old-fashioned of the three with many changes done to the costumes through time, making them closer to the kind used at the Swedish coast, rather than the others in Jämtland. The Great Jamtish part has typically old-fashioned and conservative homogeneous bunads with blue socks, red knitted caps among the males, dark bounded caps for ladies and coloured for girls. The skirts are usually of a single colour and the men have blue or black [hodden](./Hodden "Hodden") [coats](./Coat_(clothing) "Coat (clothing)"), with yellow [chamois leather](./Chamois_leather "Chamois leather") pants made from moose skin.

### Dialects

The genuine dialect of Jämtland is [Jamtish](./Jamtish "Jamtish"). The speakers of the dialect refer to it as *Jamska* ([ˈjamskɐ]), which is a definite form that translates to English as "the Jamtish". However, due to the lack of a well-established English name of the dialect both Jamtish and Jamtlandic are used.

Jamtish is in fact a group of dialects and there are distinctive dialects in every parish. Though they are usually classified in four groups; *framlänningsmålet* "the Central Jamtish tongue", *opplänningsmålet* (spoken in Western Jämtland), Southwest Jamtish and Northern Jamtish. The dialects in eastern Jämtland are sometimes considered as a fifth group of Jamtish, but also as dialects more related to the Swedish dialects spoken in [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland "Ångermanland"). In the very north of Jämtland *lidmål*, a version of [Trøndersk](./Trøndersk "Trøndersk"), is spoken. Jamtish is spoken by 50 000 people at most living in Jämtland and in other areas of Sweden, particularly the capital [Stockholm](./Stockholm "Stockholm").

### Language

Even if the Jamtish official status is a dialect many Jamtish people see it as an own language. There are multiple activists that are trying to make the Swedish government recognise Jamtish as a minority language just as [Yiddish](./Yiddish "Yiddish") or [Sami](./Sami_people "Sami people") have become one. The claimers say to look at the different words and pronunciations of them. Whether or not it is its own language has been widely debated since the early 20th century.

### Provincial character

Historically each province in Sweden has been known for a specific provincial character or *[volksgeist](./Volksgeist "Volksgeist")*. This was a field of intense research in Sweden earlier but is viewed somewhat unmodern and considered prejudice today.

The provincial character of Jämtland was often portrayed as cheerful and the population have historically been known for their hospitality. Before the dawn of the railway it was common among farmers to leave their doors unlocked when the annual summer journey to the critter houses was due, often with the table set with food for travelers.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Ostersund.JPG/250px-Ostersund.JPG)](./File:Ostersund.JPG)

Östersund was founded to stop the faring traditions in Jämtland. This happened first after the railroad was established and the city is now the trading center of Jämtland.

The faring traditions of Jämtland are also very characteristic. The Jamts were known to neglect the agriculture and instead take on long trading journeys all over Scandinavia to various [markets](./Market_(place) "Market (place)") such as the ancients ones in [Levanger](./Levanger_(town) "Levanger (town)") and [Gregorius market](./Gregorius_market?action=edit&redlink=1 "Gregorius market") on Frösön. This was regarded as sheer pleasure in itself and not as something they were obligated to do. In the middle of the 18th century Jämtland's population was roughly 20 000 and it was common that over 1 000 Jamts were present during *Marsimartnan* in Levanger, it is also claimed that the city was built solely on spikes from Jämtland before the fire in the 19th century. The journeys took place during the winters when the landscape was more accessible (when [swamps](./Swamp "Swamp"), lakes and [tarns](./Tarn_(lake) "Tarn (lake)") froze to ice) and was conducted by males, which left the females in complete charge of the [household](./Household "Household") and the [property](./Property "Property"). The journeys were well-organized [expeditions](./Exploration "Exploration") and no one traveled alone. These traditions has awarded the Jamt with traits such as enterprising and energetic. The Jamts' attempts to avoid tariffs were very successful which greatly angered Swedish officials through time. These journeys eventually stopped once the railway came, though it has recently been renewed by locals. Some say that the heritage from this age lives on, given the high number of enterprises per capita.

### Republic of Jamtland

Main article: [Republic of Jamtland](./Republic_of_Jamtland "Republic of Jamtland")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg/250px-Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg.png)](./File:Unofficial_Flag_of_Jamtland.svg)

[Flag of the Republic of Jamtland](./Flag_of_the_Republic_of_Jamtland "Flag of the Republic of Jamtland")

In the 1960s, an [independence movement](./Independence_movement "Independence movement") calling itself the "Republic of Jamtland" was created by humorist/actor/director [Yngve Gamlin](./Yngve_Gamlin "Yngve Gamlin"). Motivated on paper as an attempt to return the province to Jamtlandic control, the republic was given some form of recognition in 1967 when Mr. Gamlin was invited to an event for visiting statesmen hosted by Swedish prime minister [Tage Erlander](./Tage_Erlander "Tage Erlander"). Described in some sources as a form of criticism against [centralized](./Centralized "Centralized") Swedish government and in others as a [marketing](./Marketing "Marketing") ploy, it is likely that both played some part in its foundation (Republic officials typically describe it as "51 percent serious"). The republic has a self-styled [flag](./Flag_of_the_Republic_of_Jamtland "Flag of the Republic of Jamtland") and national anthem ([Jämtlandssången](./Jämtlandssången "Jämtlandssången")) and the independence movement hosts the annual [Storsjöyran](./Storsjöyran "Storsjöyran") event in the capital, [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund").

### Sports

Football in the province is administered by [Jämtland-Härjedalens Fotbollförbund](./Jämtland-Härjedalens_Fotbollförbund "Jämtland-Härjedalens Fotbollförbund"). The clubs overseen by the association include [Myssjö-Ovikens IF](./Myssjö-Ovikens_IF "Myssjö-Ovikens IF").

**Jämtland County** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Jämtlands län*, [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language "Southern Sami language"): *Jiemthen leene*) is a [county](./Counties_of_Sweden "Counties of Sweden") or *[län](./Län "Län")* in [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). It consists of the provinces of [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland") and [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen "Härjedalen"), along with minor parts of [Hälsingland](./Hälsingland "Hälsingland") and [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland "Ångermanland"), plus two small strips of [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden "Lapland, Sweden") and [Dalarna](./Dalarna "Dalarna"). It borders the counties of [Dalarna](./Dalarna_County "Dalarna County"), [Gävleborg](./Gävleborg_County "Gävleborg County"), [Västernorrland](./Västernorrland_County "Västernorrland County"), and [Västerbotten](./Västerbotten_County "Västerbotten County"), as well as the Norwegian county of [Trøndelag](./Trøndelag "Trøndelag"). It measures 49,443 km2 (19,090 sq mi) and constitutes 12% of Sweden's total area, making it the country's third largest county. The capital is [Östersund](./Östersund "Östersund"). The [county governor](./List_of_governors_of_Jämtland_County "List of governors of Jämtland County") and leader of the [administrative board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden"), as appointed by the Swedish government, has been Marita Ljung since 2021.[[3]](./Jämtland_County#cite_note-3)

The county was established in 1810, at the time it consisted only of the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, which is why the [coat of arms](./Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms") is a shield parted per fess with their provincial arms. [King Carl XVI Gustaf](./Carl_XVI_Gustaf "Carl XVI Gustaf") is occasionally referred to as Duke of Jämtland after his title of king.

Province
--------

For history, geography and culture, see [Jämtland](./Jämtland "Jämtland") and [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen "Härjedalen").

Jämtland County consists of primarily the provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, though minor parts of [Hälsingland](./Hälsingland "Hälsingland") and [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland "Ångermanland") are also included, along with small uninhabited areas in [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden "Lapland, Sweden") and [Dalarna](./Dalarna "Dalarna").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Administration
--------------

The main aim of the [County Administrative Board](./County_Administrative_Boards_of_Sweden "County Administrative Boards of Sweden") is to fulfill the goals set in national politics by the [Riksdag](./Riksdag "Riksdag") and the [Government](./Government_of_Sweden "Government of Sweden"), to coordinate the interests and promote the development of the county, to establish regional goals and safeguard the due process of law in the handling of each case. The County Administrative Board is a [Government Agency](./Government_Agencies_in_Sweden "Government Agencies in Sweden") headed by a Governor. See [List of Jämtland Governors](./List_of_Jämtland_Governors "List of Jämtland Governors").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Demography
----------

Jämtland County is sparsely populated and more than one-third of the population lives in the [countryside](./Countryside "Countryside"), making Jämtland County the second largest rural region in Sweden, after [Gotland County](./Gotland_County "Gotland County"). However, most of the population lives in the rather densely populated region surrounding lake [Storsjön](./Storsjön "Storsjön"), commonly called *Storsjöbygden*, "the Storsjö district/countryside".[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Politics
--------

The county is dominated by the [Swedish Social Democratic Party](./Swedish_Social_Democratic_Party "Swedish Social Democratic Party") and the [Centre Party](./Centre_Party_(Sweden) "Centre Party (Sweden)"), which is unique in Sweden, but corresponds to the situation in the bordering Norwegian county of Nord-Trøndelag. The county is rather contrastive in the political field. While a majority of the municipalities are governed by [liberal](./Liberalism "Liberalism")-[conservative](./Conservatism "Conservatism") ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *borgerlig*, lit. "[bourgeois](./Bourgeois "Bourgeois")") majorities or by coalitions overstepping the bloc border, the [county council](./County_Councils_of_Sweden "County Councils of Sweden") is controlled by a [red-green](./Red-Greens_(Sweden) "Red-Greens (Sweden)") majority and the Social Democrats receive two out of four [mandates](./Mandate_(politics) "Mandate (politics)") to the [Riksdag](./Riksdag "Riksdag").

Heraldry
--------

The arms for the County of Jämtland is a combination of the arms of [Heraldry of Jämtland](./Heraldry_of_Jämtland?action=edit&redlink=1 "Heraldry of Jämtland") and [Heraldry of Härjedalen](./Heraldry_of_Härjedalen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Heraldry of Härjedalen"). When it is shown with a royal crown it represents the County Administrative Board. Blazon: "Parted per fess, the arms of Jämtland and the arms of Härjedalen."

**Bräcke Municipality** ([Swedish](./Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Bräcke kommun*) is a [municipality](./Municipalities_of_Sweden "Municipalities of Sweden") in [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County "Jämtland County") in northern [Sweden](./Sweden "Sweden"). Its [seat](./Administrative_centre "Administrative centre") is located in [Bräcke](./Bräcke "Bräcke").

The present municipality was formed in 1974 when "old" Bräcke Municipality was amalgamated with Kälarne and Revsund. The three former municipalities had been created in 1952. The number of original entities (as of 1863) were six. Due to the declining population in the area further amalgamations have been proposed, but rejected.
