It borders [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen \"Härjedalen\") and [Medelpad](./Medelpad \"Medelpad\") to the south, [Ångermanland](./Ångermanland \"Ångermanland\") to the east, [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden \"Lapland, Sweden\") to the north and [Trøndelag](./Trøndelag \"Trøndelag\") and [Norway](./Norway \"Norway\") to the west. Jämtland covers an area of 34,009 square kilometres, 8.3% of Sweden\\'s total area and is the second largest province in Sweden. It has a population of 115,331,[[1]](./Jämtland#cite_note-population-1) the majority of whom live in *Storsjöbygden*, the area surrounding lake [Storsjön](./Storsjön \"Storsjön\"). [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\") is Jämtland\\'s only city and is the [24th most populous city in Sweden](./List_of_cities_in_Sweden_by_population \"List of cities in Sweden by population\"). The historical province is one of the least densely populated.\\n\\nJämtland was originally an autonomous [republic](./Republic \"Republic\"),[[2]](./Jämtland#cite_note-republic-2) its own [nation](./Nation \"Nation\")[[2]](./Jämtland#cite_note-republic-2) with its own [law](./Law \"Law\"), [currency](./Currency \"Currency\")[[3]](./Jämtland#cite_note-3) and [parliament](./Parliament \"Parliament\"). Jämtland was conquered by [Norway](./Norway \"Norway\") in 1178 and stayed Norwegian for over 450 years until it was ceded to Sweden in 1645. The province has since been Swedish for roughly 370 years, though the population did not gain Swedish citizenship until 1699. The province\\'s identity is manifested with the humorous culture and marketing concept of a [republic](./Republic_of_Jamtland \"Republic of Jamtland\") within the kingdom of Sweden, although this is only done semi-seriously.[[4]](./Jämtland#cite_note-4)\\n\\nHistorically, socially and politically Jämtland has been a special territory between Norway and Sweden. This in itself is symbolized in the province\\'s coat of arms where Jämtland, the silver moose, is threatened from the east and from the west. During the unrest period in Jämtland\\'s history (1563–1677) it shifted alignment between the two states through occupations no less than 13 times.[[5]](./Jämtland#cite_note-5)\\n\\nEtymology\\n---------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen.jpg/250px-Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6stenen.jpg)](./File:Frösöstenen.jpg)\\n\\nFrösö Runestone\\n\\n\\n\\nMain article: [Etymology of Jämtland](./Etymology_of_Jämtland \"Etymology of Jämtland\")\\n\\nJämtland\\'s name derives from its inhabitants, the Jamts.[[6]](./Jämtland#cite_note-etymology-6) The name can be traced back to Europe\\'s northernmost [runestone](./Runestone \"Runestone\"), the [Frösö Runestone](./Frösö_Runestone \"Frösö Runestone\") from the 11th century, where it is found as *eotalont* (normalized [Old Norse](./Old_Norse \"Old Norse\"): *Jamtaland*). The [root](./Root_(linguistics) \"Root (linguistics)\") of Jamt ([Old West Norse](./Old_West_Norse \"Old West Norse\"): *jamti*), and thus Jämtland, derives from the [Proto-Germanic](./Proto-Germanic \"Proto-Germanic\") [word stem](./Word_stem \"Word stem\") *emat-* meaning persistent, efficient, enduring and hardworking.[[6]](./Jämtland#cite_note-etymology-6) The [Proto-Norse](./Proto-Norse \"Proto-Norse\") [prefix](./Prefix \"Prefix\") *eota* (*jamta*) is a [genitive](./Genitive \"Genitive\") [plural](./Plural \"Plural\") case.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Olav_den_helliges_saga_-_Torodd_Arnljott_Geline_-_H._Egedius_-_H._Egedius.jpg/250px-Olav_den_helliges_saga_-_Torodd_Arnljott_Geline_-_H._Egedius_-_H._Egedius.jpg)](./File:Olav_den_helliges_saga_-_Torodd_Arnljott_Geline_-_H._Egedius_-_H._Egedius.jpg)\\n\\nJämtland does not mean \"the even country\" but rather \"Jamts\\' land\". In this picture the [Viking](./Viking \"Viking\") Arnljot Gelline from Jämtland is seen moving through the landscape.\\n\\nIt is not known how the Jamts got their name. One possible explanation is presented in the [Icelandic](./Iceland \"Iceland\") work *[Heimskringla](./Heimskringla \"Heimskringla\")* from the 13th century. In the [Saga of Håkon Góði](./Heimskringla#Contents \"Heimskringla\"), [Snorri Sturluson](./Snorri_Sturluson \"Snorri Sturluson\") narrates about Kettil Jamti, a son of Anund [Jarl](./Jarl_(title) \"Jarl (title)\") from [Sparbu](./Sparbu \"Sparbu\") in Trøndelag who fled from Norway when [Harald Fairhair](./Harald_I_of_Norway \"Harald I of Norway\") united the country with brute force in the 9th century. His descendants then came to bear his [name](./Family_name \"Family name\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] An alternative explanation comes from the excessive iron production that took place in the province before the [Viking Age](./Viking_Age \"Viking Age\"). A [folk etymological](./Folk_etymology \"Folk etymology\") theory is that the name ought to have something to do with the \"even\" (as in level or flat) parts around the [lake](./Lake \"Lake\") [Storsjön](./Storsjön \"Storsjön\"). This theory is based on the similarity between the Swedish words *jämt* (from *emat-*) and *jämnt* (from Germanic *\\\\*ebna*, \"even\").[[6]](./Jämtland#cite_note-etymology-6)\\n\\nThe name Jämtland with an [Ä](./Ä \"Ä\") is a 20th-century Swedish alteration of the older spelling *Jemtland*. Localities settled by Jamtish emigrants such as [Jemtland](./Jemtland,_Ringsaker?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Jemtland, Ringsaker\") in [Ringsaker Municipality](./Ringsaker_Municipality \"Ringsaker Municipality\"), Norway and [Jemtland](./Jemtland,_Maine \"Jemtland, Maine\") in [Maine](./Maine \"Maine\"), United States were founded before the alteration occurred. In the nearby Norwegian province of Trøndelag old settlements such as [Jamtøya](./Jamtøya?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Jamtøya\"), [Jamtgarden](./Jamtgarden?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Jamtgarden\") and [Jamtåsen](./Jamtåsen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Jamtåsen\") all use the prefix *Jamt-*, just like the regional name, however the [Trøndersk](./Trøndersk \"Trøndersk\") name for Jämtland is *Jamtlainn*,[[7]](./Jämtland#cite_note-verdal-7) whilst the Jamtish name is *Jamtland*. As the d is silent the form *Jamtlann* is also common. The regional name *Jamtland* has only status as an official form in [Nynorsk](./Nynorsk \"Nynorsk\")[[7]](./Jämtland#cite_note-verdal-7) and [Icelandic](./Icelandic_language \"Icelandic language\"),[[8]](./Jämtland#cite_note-8) but is popularly used among locals which is one of the reasons as to why the regional museum was given the dialectal name [Jamtli](./Jamtli \"Jamtli\") (Swedish *jämtsk backsluttning*),[[9]](./Jämtland#cite_note-9) \"Jamtish hillside\".\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n|  | This section **contains an excessive amount of intricate [detail](./Wikipedia:DETAIL \"Wikipedia:DETAIL\")**. Please help [improve it](//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=J%C3%A4mtland&action=edit) by [spinning off](./Wikipedia:Content_forks#Article_spinoffs:_.22Summary_style.22_meta-articles_and_summary_sections \"Wikipedia:Content forks\") or [relocating](./Wikipedia:Handling_trivia#Recommendations_for_handling_trivia \"Wikipedia:Handling trivia\") relevant information and removing excessive detail that goes against [Wikipedia\\'s inclusion policy](./Wikipedia:What_Wikipedia_is_not \"Wikipedia:What Wikipedia is not\"). *(October 2020)* *([Learn how and when to remove this message](./Help:Maintenance_template_removal \"Help:Maintenance template removal\"))* |\\n\\n\\n\\nMain article: [History of Jämtland](./History_of_Jämtland \"History of Jämtland\")\\n\\n### Prehistory\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Elanden_van_Glosa_20juli2005.jpg/330px-Elanden_van_Glosa_20juli2005.jpg)](./File:Elanden_van_Glosa_20juli2005.jpg)\\n\\nPetroglyphs in [Glösa](./Glösa \"Glösa\"), made approximately 5,000 years ago, displaying primarily moose. Several internal [organs](./Organ_(anatomy) \"Organ (anatomy)\") have been painted out. The carvings are very similar to the ones found in [Moelv](./Moelv_(Trøndelag)?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Moelv (Trøndelag)\") in Trøndelag and also resemble the [cave art](./Cave_art \"Cave art\") in [Altamira](./Cave_of_Altamira \"Cave of Altamira\"), [Spain](./Spain \"Spain\"). A carved ram from Glösa appears in [Krokom\\'s](./Krokom_Municipality \"Krokom Municipality\") [coat of arms](./Coat_of_arms \"Coat of arms\").\\n\\nSome finds from the time before humans have been discovered in Jämtland, most notably the remains from a [woolly mammoth](./Woolly_mammoth \"Woolly mammoth\") in [Pilgrimstad](./Pilgrimstad \"Pilgrimstad\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nThe first humans came to Jämtland from the west across [the Keel](./Scandinavian_Mountains \"Scandinavian Mountains\") approximately 7000–6000 [BC](./Before_Christ \"Before Christ\"), after the [last ice age](./Last_glacial_period \"Last glacial period\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The climate was at the time much warmer than today and trees such as [oak](./Oak \"Oak\") were growing at the top of today\\'s mountains. Several thousand archaeological remains have been located in the province, predominantly near old camp-sites, beaches and lakes. The oldest settlement found is located at [Foskvattnet](./Foskvattnet?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Foskvattnet\"), not far way from the so-called [Fosna culture](./Fosna-Hensbacka_culture \"Fosna-Hensbacka culture\"), this settlement has been dated to 6600 BC. In Jämtland the moose was the dominant prey, which is clearly shown on [petroglyphs](./Petroglyph \"Petroglyph\") and rock paintings in for example [Gärde](./Gärde \"Gärde\") and [Glösa](./Glösa \"Glösa\"). Jämtland has over 20,000 documented [ancient monuments](./Ancient_monument \"Ancient monument\"), the oldest one being an arrowhead found in Åflo near [Kaxås](./Kaxås \"Kaxås\") in [Offerdal](./Offerdal \"Offerdal\") parish possibly older than 8,000 years, which would make it one of the oldest Stone Age finds in all of Sweden.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nRock paintings found in Jämtland often collocates with various [trapping pits](./Trapping_pit \"Trapping pit\") and well over 10,000 pits used for hunting have been located, which is much more than any other Scandinavian region. Trapping or hunting pits were placed in areas in close proximity of the hunted animal in question, usually in known places where the animals moved. Because of this there are several places where pits have been dug separately in lines stretching on for miles throughout the landscape. Several [place names](./Place_name \"Place name\") in Jämtland still display the significance these pits had to the tribes.\\n\\n|  |  |  |  |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n|  |  |  |  |\\n| Trapping pit | A moose painted with [red ochre](./Red_ochre \"Red ochre\") near [Fångsjön](./Fångsjön?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Fångsjön\") | Fångsjön rock art site, dated to 2500-2000 BC | Burned rocks in northern Jämtland |\\n\\nA Jamtish [Neolithic](./Neolithic \"Neolithic\") culture emerged during late [Roman Iron Age](./Roman_Iron_Age \"Roman Iron Age\") in [Storsjöbygden](./Storsjöbygden?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Storsjöbygden\"), although the hunter-gatherers had come in contact with this lifestyle long before they settled down themselves. Since the hunts were rich and successful in Jämtland, it took a long time before a change occurred.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nThe [Neolithic Revolution](./Neolithic_Revolution \"Neolithic Revolution\") happened quickly once initiated since the [Trønders](./Trønder \"Trønder\") had been farmers for a long time and some of the Jamts had already begun [herding](./Herding \"Herding\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The Jamtish farmers grew first and foremost [barley](./Barley \"Barley\"), although [palynological](./Palynological \"Palynological\") study also show [hemp](./Hemp \"Hemp\"). At the end of the 4th century a [fortress](./Fortress \"Fortress\"), [Mjälleborgen](./Mjälleborgen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Mjälleborgen\"), was established on Frösön to control the iron production and [trade](./Trade \"Trade\") that took place. At the same time [kurgans](./Kurgan \"Kurgan\") start appearing in the Jamtish landscape, just like in [Bertnem](./Bertnem?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Bertnem\") in Trøndelag and [Högom](./Högom?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Högom\") in Medelpad. The western influence from Trøndelag through Jämtland to Norrland was at the time extensive.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.JPG/330px-Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.JPG)](./File:Frösön.JPG)\\n\\nFrösön during winter. This island, named after [Freyr](./Freyr \"Freyr\"), the Norse god of [fecundity](./Fecundity \"Fecundity\") and [love](./Love \"Love\"), was the regional centre of Jämtland for ages.\\n\\nThe expansion of settlement was somewhat halted in the 7th century and Mjälleborgen was abandoned in the 8th century. A [human migration](./Human_migration \"Human migration\") occurred at the same time and the people concentrated themselves around Storsjön with villages such as [Frösön](./Frösön \"Frösön\"), [Brunflo](./Brunflo \"Brunflo\"), [Rödön](./Rödön \"Rödön\"), [Hackås](./Hackås \"Hackås\"), [Lockne](./Lockne?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Lockne\") and [Näs](./Näs_(village)?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Näs (village)\") being larger communities. Storsjöbygden became an [oasis](./Oasis \"Oasis\") in the middle of the Scandinavian inland, surrounded by dense forest. [Horses](./Horse \"Horse\") were the only reliable means of transportation and therefore a necessity.\\n\\nDuring the [Viking Age](./Viking_Age \"Viking Age\"), the settlement in the province grew. This confirms the sagas written by [Snorri Sturluson](./Snorri_Sturluson \"Snorri Sturluson\"), where he narrates about the Vikings who fled from [Harald Fairhair](./Harald_Fairhair \"Harald Fairhair\") and Norway and took residence in Jämtland, just like many Norwegians at the same time fled and colonized Iceland. When a [climate change](./Climate_change_(general_concept) \"Climate change (general concept)\") (which later resulted in the [Medieval Warm Period](./Medieval_Warm_Period \"Medieval Warm Period\")) took place, Frösön acquired the position as regional centre. The warmer climate made the [agriculture](./Agriculture \"Agriculture\") flourish, the stock-raising and the special inland Scandinavian [herding](./Herding \"Herding\") or \"livestock drifting\", *buföring*, was developed further. This is especially true for the southern parts of Jämtland when the so-called \"[fell](./Fell \"Fell\") cow\" was introduced. The hunt for moose and other wild animals increased during this period. [Religiously](./Religion \"Religion\") the Jamts had abandoned the [indigenous Germanic tribal religion](./Norse_paganism \"Norse paganism\") in favour of the Christian faith. In religious practice, Jämtland was dominated by the older [Vanir](./Vanir \"Vanir\") gods ([Freyr](./Freyr \"Freyr\"), [Njord](./Njord \"Njord\"), etc.), although the [Æsir](./Æsir \"Æsir\") were also worshiped.[*[clarification needed](./Wikipedia:Please_clarify \"Wikipedia:Please clarify\")*]\\n\\nAs the population continued to grow, the Jamts established a [Thing (assembly)](./Thing_(assembly) \"Thing (assembly)\"), just like other Germanic tribes. [Jamtamót](./Jamtamót \"Jamtamót\") came into existence shortly after the world\\'s oldest parliament, the Icelandic [Althing](./Althing \"Althing\"), was instituted in 930 CE.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Jamtamót is unique in Scandinavia since it is the only one referred to as *mót* instead of *þing*, although they have the same meaning.\\n\\n### Medieval period\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/8/8b/Seal_of_Jamtland.svg/250px-Seal_of_Jamtland.svg.png)](./File:Seal_of_Jamtland.svg)\\n\\n[Magnus VI of Norway](./Magnus_VI_of_Norway \"Magnus VI of Norway\"), named “the law-mender”, gave Jämtland its first known [seal](./Seal_(emblem) \"Seal (emblem)\") 1274. [The Norwegian Lion](./Coat_of_arms_of_Norway \"Coat of arms of Norway\") has an [Olav](./Olaf_II_of_Norway \"Olaf II of Norway\")-axe and the shield is crownless, which indicates that it is a “realm seal”[[10]](./Jämtland#cite_note-10) and not a province dito. Besides Jämtland, only the [Orkney islands](./Orkney \"Orkney\") received this type of seal.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Mattmar_kyrka.jpg/250px-Mattmar_kyrka.jpg)](./File:Mattmar_kyrka.jpg)\\n\\nMedieval church in [Mattmar](./Mattmar?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Mattmar\")\\n\\nJämtland was [Christianized](./Christianization_of_Scandinavia \"Christianization of Scandinavia\") in the middle of the 11th century when the [Frösö Runestone](./Frösö_Runestone \"Frösö Runestone\") appeared (the only one in the world that tells about the christening of a country), shortly after [Olaf II of Norway](./Olaf_II_of_Norway \"Olaf II of Norway\") died in the [Battle of Stiklestad](./Battle_of_Stiklestad \"Battle of Stiklestad\") just west of Jämtland. During this period Jämtland turned into a Christian region and the first church, [Västerhus chapel](./Västerhus_chapel?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Västerhus chapel\") was built shortly after the runestone appeared.\\n\\nAccording to [Snorri Sturluson](./Snorri_Sturluson \"Snorri Sturluson\")\\'s Sagas[*[which?](./Wikipedia:Avoid_weasel_words \"Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words\")*] the Jamts sometimes paid taxes to Norwegian kings such as [Håkon Adalsteinsfostre](./Haakon_I_of_Norway \"Haakon I of Norway\") and [Øystein Magnusson](./Eystein_I_of_Norway \"Eystein I of Norway\") for protection. The Sagas also mentions that the Jamts at one occasion also paid taxes to a king in [Svealand](./Svealand \"Svealand\"). The Sagas reliability on the matter has been defined as low.[[11]](./Jämtland#cite_note-11) In the oldest written source for Norway, *[Historia Norwegiæ](./Historia_Norwegiæ \"Historia Norwegiæ\")*, it is however clearly stated that Norway borders in the north-east to Jämtland.\\n\\nDuring the [civil war era in Norway](./Civil_war_era_in_Norway \"Civil war era in Norway\") Jämtland was defeated by king [Sverre of Norway](./Sverre_of_Norway \"Sverre of Norway\") after losing the [Battle of Storsjön](./Battle_of_Storsjön \"Battle of Storsjön\"). This was the last war fought by the Jamts under their own elected leaders.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The consequences of this defeat was less [autonomy](./Autonomy \"Autonomy\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Jämtland never became a fully integrated part of Norway and had the same status in the Kingdom of Norway (872–1397) as the Atlantic isles like [Shetland](./Shetland \"Shetland\") and [Orkney](./Orkney \"Orkney\"), even though Jämtland was connected by land with the rest of Norway. This is clearly shown when [Haakon V of Norway](./Haakon_V_of_Norway \"Haakon V of Norway\") refers to Jämtland as his \"eastern realm — *öystræ rikinu*\".[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Iempihia%2C_Carta_Marina.jpg/250px-Iempihia%2C_Carta_Marina.jpg)](./File:Iempihia,_Carta_Marina.jpg)\\n\\nA detail from [Olaus Magnus](./Olaus_Magnus \"Olaus Magnus\")’ *[Carta Marina](./Carta_Marina \"Carta Marina\")* (1539). Jämtland is [Latinized](./Latinisation_(literature) \"Latinisation (literature)\") as \"Iempihia\".\\n\\n### Turbulent times\\n\\nAfter Norway was forced into a [personal union](./Personal_union \"Personal union\") with [Denmark](./Denmark \"Denmark\") ([Denmark-Norway](./Denmark-Norway \"Denmark-Norway\")) in 1536 Jämtland came to be governed from [Copenhagen](./Copenhagen \"Copenhagen\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] When the [reformation](./Protestant_Reformation \"Protestant Reformation\") ([Catholicism](./Catholicism \"Catholicism\") survived in some places into the 17th century) was forced upon the population when the kings took control of the church. Sweden\\'s separation from the [Kalmar Union](./Kalmar_Union \"Kalmar Union\") transferred Jämtland from a central Scandinavian region into a border region between two aggressive states. This eventually led to conflict, first in 1563 during the [Nordic Seven Years\\' War](./Nordic_Seven_Years\\'_War \"Nordic Seven Years\\' War\") (after which Jämtland was put under the [diocese of Nidaros](./Diocese_of_Nidaros \"Diocese of Nidaros\")), then in 1611 during the [Kalmar War](./Kalmar_War \"Kalmar War\"). Conflict continued and Jämtland was occupied yet again in 1644 during the [Hannibal War](./Hannibal_War \"Hannibal War\") by Swedish forces under the command of [Henrik Fleming](./Henrik_Fleming \"Henrik Fleming\"). The Swedish troops were however quickly driven out by Norwegians and locals.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Sweden did however win that war in the south and received Jämtland as a part of the [Treaty of Brömsebro](./Second_Treaty_of_Brömsebro_(1645) \"Second Treaty of Brömsebro (1645)\") in 1645.[[12]](./Jämtland#cite_note-12)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Jemtland.png/500px-Jemtland.png)](./File:Jemtland.png)\\n\\nJämtland\\xa0– the land in between (*mitt emellom*). There are only a few kilometers to the [Bothnian Sea](./Bothnian_Sea \"Bothnian Sea\") as well as to the [Norwegian Sea](./Norwegian_Sea \"Norwegian Sea\"), which has led Jämtland often to be occupied by foreign powers. This map from 1905 shows the then [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County \"Jämtland County\"), comprising Jämtland and [Härjedalen](./Härjedalen \"Härjedalen\").\\n\\nAfter this Denmark-Norway tried to regain the province, first in 1657 ([Dano-Swedish war of 1657](./Dano-Swedish_War_(1657-1658) \"Dano-Swedish War (1657-1658)\")) where the Norwegians were hailed as liberators.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Then for a longer period in 1677 with the *[conquest of Jemtland](./Conquest_of_Jemtland \"Conquest of Jemtland\")*. The Jamts conducted [snapphane](./Snapphane \"Snapphane\") (guerilla) warfare against the Swedish army and during this time a Jamt from [Lockne](./Lockne?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Lockne\"), the first known Jamtish poet, wrote a scurrilous song that was sung throughout the province during the war. It involved the Swedish governor of Jämtland and he had the song translated into [Swedish](./Swedish_language \"Swedish language\") from [Jamtish](./Jamtish \"Jamtish\") and sent to the king. The last segment of the song was the most derisive one (direct English translation to the right):\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| *Vii hafva nu lefft uti 30 åhrs tijdh*  *allt under Sveriges chrona*  *uti strijdh och tyrani ingen persohn att skona.*  *Tiig vari priss o Gudh, vår vän,*  *som gaf oss danske kungen igen*  *med gledie.* | *We have now lived for 30 years time*  *certainly under the Swedish crown*  *through battle and tyranny no person to spare*  *You be praised oh God, our friend*  *who gave us the Danish king again*  *with joy.* |\\n\\nThe conquest failed and once Jämtland was in Swedish hands a Swedification process began.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The [Diocese of Härnösand](./Diocese_of_Härnösand \"Diocese of Härnösand\") was instituted at the Swedish coast. Schools were established (to direct the Jamts away from Trondheim). The population did not receive Swedish citizenship until 1699. Thus the Jamts were the last people from an acquired territory in Sweden to become Swedish.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\nThe Jamtish people maintained some [self-governance](./Self-governance \"Self-governance\"). The Jamtamót had been transformed into a Danish [landsting](./Thing_(assembly) \"Thing (assembly)\") in the early 16th century. Even though it was banned in the end of the same century, it continued to be held in secret.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] After the transition to Sweden some parts were transmitted[*[clarification needed](./Wikipedia:Please_clarify \"Wikipedia:Please clarify\")*] into a Swedish *landsjämnadsting*.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/D%C3%B6da_fallet_20061014.jpg/330px-D%C3%B6da_fallet_20061014.jpg)](./File:Döda_fallet_20061014.jpg)\\n\\nThe \"dead waterfall\" in the autumn of 2006.\\n\\nSweden\\'s intentions in the province were first and foremost focused on defense, which led to a burden on the Jamtish farmers.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The Jamts managed to enforce a treaty in 1688 which stated that Jamts were under no circumstances obligated to defend anything but their own province. This treaty was eventually broken by king [Charles XII](./Charles_XII_of_Sweden \"Charles XII of Sweden\") and Jamts participated in [Carl Gustaf Armfeldt](./Carl_Gustaf_Armfeldt \"Carl Gustaf Armfeldt\")\\'s Norwegian campaign during the [Great Northern War](./Great_Northern_War \"Great Northern War\"). The campaign was unsuccessful and when Charles XII died in southern Norway Armfeldt marched back to Jämtland. On [New Year\\'s Eve](./New_Year\\'s_Eve \"New Year\\'s Eve\") 1718 a massive [blizzard](./Blizzard \"Blizzard\") arose and over 3,000 [Caroleans](./Caroleans \"Caroleans\") succumbed in Jämtland\\'s mountains mostly due to poor clothing.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] The time that followed \"the [Age of Liberty](./Age_of_Liberty \"Age of Liberty\")\" brought changes to the province\\'s agriculture, with significances such as the [potato](./Potato \"Potato\") and better [granaries](./Granary \"Granary\") through national politics. The [standard of living](./Standard_of_living \"Standard of living\") was greatly improved during this period. However, the visions and ideas behind the improvements also led to one of the greatest environmental disasters in Scandinavia when the lake [Ragundasjön](./Ragundasjön \"Ragundasjön\") was drained and the great rapid Gedungsen cut off, creating the so-called \"[dead waterfall](./Döda_Fallet \"Döda Fallet\")\". It was the result of a project that sought to circumvent the obstacle posed by the waterfall for [timber](./Timber \"Timber\") transportation on [Indalsälven](./Indalsälven \"Indalsälven\").\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Vy_%C3%B6ver_%C3%96stersund_fr%C3%A5n_Gustavsbergsbacken_p%C3%A5_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg/330px-Vy_%C3%B6ver_%C3%96stersund_fr%C3%A5n_Gustavsbergsbacken_p%C3%A5_Fr%C3%B6s%C3%B6n.jpg)](./File:Vy_över_Östersund_från_Gustavsbergsbacken_på_Frösön.jpg)\\n\\n[Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), the winter city.\\n\\n### Modern period\\n\\nIn order to end the free trade conducted by \"faring-men\" or \"faring-farmers\" (*fælmännan* or *fælbönnran* in dialect), Jämtland\\'s first and only city, [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), was founded by [Gustav III](./Gustav_III \"Gustav III\") 1786, though plans had existed since the province was seceded. It took almost one hundred years after this before the province began industrializing when the rail road [Mittbanan](./Mittbanan \"Mittbanan\")-[Meråkerbanen](./Meråkerbanen \"Meråkerbanen\") was established between [Sundsvall](./Sundsvall \"Sundsvall\"), Östersund and [Trondheim](./Trondheim \"Trondheim\"). This evolved the [logging](./Logging \"Logging\") process and also led to more people migrating to Jämtland, not to mention all the tourists who came for the \"fresh air\". As a side effect the rail road also meant the end of the faring traditions.\\nAfter the unsuccessful (or successful, depending on the viewer) channelling of Gedungsen Jämtland\\'s rich forests could be used in [sawmills](./Sawmill \"Sawmill\") along the coast. A great deal of the forest was sold to large corporations since for the first time in history the farmers could earn money from their forests.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c3/Str%C3%B6msund30-tal.jpg/250px-Str%C3%B6msund30-tal.jpg)](./File:Strömsund30-tal.jpg)\\n\\nThe town [Strömsund](./Strömsund \"Strömsund\") in northern Jämtland in the 1930s.\\n\\nIn the late 19th century the province was struck by [social movements](./Social_movement \"Social movement\"). In Jämtland the \"[free minded](./Liberalism \"Liberalism\")\" [Good Templar movement](./International_Organisation_of_Good_Templars \"International Organisation of Good Templars\") (a part of the [temperance movement](./Temperance_movement \"Temperance movement\")) came to dominate completely, in fact, the movement drew its strongest support (in relation to the population) in Jämtland in the entire world, and it was also here, in Östersund, that the world\\'s largest order house was built. Jämtland failed to industrialize, mostly due to the residents opposition to industries, which were seen as the destroyers of society. Keeping Jämtland as a clean environment, but also making it a region of [raw material](./Raw_material \"Raw material\") extraction. Due to the rail road the city of Östersund quickly grew with settlers arriving from the countryside and southern Sweden, giving it the true character of a city, rather than a mere village with city status. The rise of Östersund brought a more excessive trade than before, [handicrafts](./Handicraft \"Handicraft\") etc. Just like in the rest of the [Western world](./Western_world \"Western world\") a modernisation process started in the 20th century. New items such as [cars](./Car \"Car\"), [fridges](./Fridge \"Fridge\"), [television](./Television \"Television\") etc. made their way into people\\'s lives.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Oviken.jpg/330px-Oviken.jpg)](./File:Oviken.jpg)\\n\\nHouses on the countryside in Oviken, southern Jämtland.\\n\\nWith the establishment of the [socialist](./Socialism \"Socialism\") [Folkhemmet](./Folkhemmet \"Folkhemmet\") (*the people\\'s home*) and the [Rehn-Meidner model](./Rehn-Meidner_model \"Rehn-Meidner model\") Jämtland became a true neglected area in Sweden. The model deemed it necessary to concentrate the Swedish population in cities, at the coast and in the south. Jämtland an inland region in Norrland with the largest part of the population living in the countryside in Sweden was by far the most unprofitable region one could imagine. When the politics were launched Jämtland experienced the largest population loss in modern Swedish history. Local companies were forced into bankruptcy and unemployed people were encouraged to move to cities at the coast or in the south through subsidies and governmental commercials. At the same time taxes were rising and the [public sector](./Public_sector \"Public sector\") growing. Opposition to the loss of population and the [centralist](./Centralization \"Centralization\") plans among officials regarding [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County \"Jämtland County\") led to the creation of the *Republic of Jamtland* ([see below](./Jämtland#Republic_of_Jamtland)).\\n\\n### Subdivision and law\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Andersonbrygga.JPG/330px-Andersonbrygga.JPG)](./File:Andersonbrygga.JPG)\\n\\nThe jetty on Andersön island\\n\\nJämtland was originally divided into four parts, so called farthings (*fjalingan* or *fjålingan* in Jamtish), just like Iceland (*fjórðungr* in [Icelandic](./Icelandic_language \"Icelandic language\")). This division is similar to the [hundred subdivision](./Hundred_(country_subdivision) \"Hundred (country subdivision)\") the rest of Scandinavia had. Just like on Iceland these farthings were named after [cardinal directions](./Cardinal_direction \"Cardinal direction\"). Exactly how the borders for each farthing went is unknown although it has been suggested that they all reached Storsjön in the center of the province. The eastern farthing at [Brunflo](./Brunflo \"Brunflo\"), the western from [Trångsviken](./Trångsviken \"Trångsviken\") to the [Rödö peninsula](./Rödö_peninsula?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Rödö peninsula\") and the south farthing from [Oviken](./Oviken \"Oviken\") and [Hackås](./Hackås \"Hackås\") and southwards. The northern farthing is assumed to have covered all the northern parts in addition to all the islands in Storsjön (like Frösön, [Norderön](./Norderön?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Norderön\"), [Andersön](./Andersön?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Andersön\") etc.) and [Mörsil](./Mörsil \"Mörsil\") plus [Hallen parish](./Hallen_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Hallen parish\") all the way to *[Oviksfjällen](./Oviksfjällen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Oviksfjällen\")*.\\n\\nThe farthings were lesser administrative regions, more or less [juridical districts](./Jurisdiction \"Jurisdiction\") with their own assemblies, all parallel with the common assembly on Frösön. The old [law](./Law \"Law\") used in Jämtland is the so-called [Jamtish Law](./Jamtish_Law?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Jamtish Law\"), referred to in old documents as e.g. *Jamptskum laughom*. Old documents also makes reference to a specific law book — *Jamskre loghbok*.[[13]](./Jämtland#cite_note-13) The law book has never been recovered and it is assumed to have been destroyed in the 16th century, or never having existed at all. Nevertheless, the Jamtish law was either the same, or strongly influenced by the [Frostating](./Frostating \"Frostating\") law applied on Trøndelag.\\n\\nWhen [Magnus the law-mender](./Magnus_VI_of_Norway \"Magnus VI of Norway\") became the king of Norway he instituted a national law for Norway in 1276, however Jämtland was not applied by this law. Jämtland came under this law either in 1365 or in the middle of the 16th century.[[14]](./Jämtland#cite_note-14) The divisions by farthings were replaced in the 16th century by [Court Districts](./Category:Provincial_Court_Districts_of_Sweden \"Category:Provincial Court Districts of Sweden\"), shortly after Jämtland got its own Norwegian law thing.\\n\\nCourt Districts in Jämtland\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Are2o.jpg/500px-Are2o.jpg)](./File:Are2o.jpg)\\n\\nSomeone from western Jämtland lives *opp i lännan*, “up in the lands”, which alludes to the high position this region is known for. This is hinted by [Åreskutan](./Åreskutan \"Åreskutan\") behind the old church of Åre in this picture.\\n\\n:   [Berg Court District](./Berg_Court_District \"Berg Court District\")\\n:   [Brunflo Court District](./Brunflo_Court_District \"Brunflo Court District\")\\n:   [Hackås Court District](./Hackås_Court_District \"Hackås Court District\")\\n:   [Hallen Court District](./Hallen_Court_District \"Hallen Court District\")\\n:   [Hammerdal Court District](./Hammerdal_Court_District \"Hammerdal Court District\")\\n:   [Lits Court District](./Lits_Court_District \"Lits Court District\")\\n:   [Offerdal Court District](./Offerdal_Court_District \"Offerdal Court District\")\\n:   [Oviken Court District](./Oviken_Court_District \"Oviken Court District\")\\n:   [Ragunda Court District](./Ragunda_Court_District \"Ragunda Court District\")\\n:   [Revsund Court District](./Revsund_Court_District \"Revsund Court District\")\\n:   [Rödön Court District](./Rödön_Court_District \"Rödön Court District\")\\n:   [Sunne Court District](./Sunne_Court_District \"Sunne Court District\")\\n:   [Undersåker Court District](./Undersåker_Court_District \"Undersåker Court District\")\\n\\nThere is also an historical subdivision of Jämtland in Jamtlandic. One area is referred to as *Nol i bygdom* \"the north countryside\" and consist of [Lit](./Lits_Court_District \"Lits Court District\")-[Hammerdal](./Hammerdal_Court_District \"Hammerdal Court District\") and the area further north. *Sö i bygdom* \"the south countryside\" or *Sunna sjön* consists of the area just south of Storsjön; [Oviken](./Oviken_Court_District \"Oviken Court District\"), [Berg](./Berg_Court_District \"Berg Court District\"), [Sunne](./Sunne_Court_District \"Sunne Court District\") and [Hallen](./Hallen_Court_District \"Hallen Court District\"). *Öst i bygdom* (also *ast, äst, ust, åst* etc. instead of \"öst\") for eastern Jämtland, mainly [Ragunda](./Ragunda_Court_District \"Ragunda Court District\"), [Revsund](./Revsund_Court_District \"Revsund Court District\") and [Brunflo](./Brunflo_Court_District \"Brunflo Court District\"). *Opp i lännan* \"up in the lands\" refers to western Jämtland, [Undersåker](./Undersåker_Court_District \"Undersåker Court District\") and [Offerdal](./Offerdal_Court_District \"Offerdal Court District\"). *Fram på lännan* \"the front\", \"central lands\" or *in på lännan* \"in on the lands\" consists of the area around Storsjön like Frösön, [Rödön](./Rödön_Court_District \"Rödön Court District\") etc. A person from this area is called a *framlänning* \"front lander\".\\n\\n### Churches\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/H%C3%A5sj%C3%B6_Gamla_Kyrka.jpg/250px-H%C3%A5sj%C3%B6_Gamla_Kyrka.jpg)](./File:Håsjö_Gamla_Kyrka.jpg)\\n\\nThe old church in Håsjö. The churches were almost always placed centrally where everybody could gaze upon them. A copy of this [bell tower](./Bell_tower \"Bell tower\"), typical for Jämtland, is located at [Skansen](./Skansen \"Skansen\") in [Stockholm](./Stockholm \"Stockholm\").\\n\\nAfter the conversion to [Christianity](./Christianity \"Christianity\") several [parishes](./Parish \"Parish\") (so called *socknar*, related to \"seek\") were established in Jämtland, these are now replaced by over 40 *församlingar*, meaning \"assemblage\". These are organized by so-called *kontrakt* \"contracts\", collaboration units within the [Swedish church\\'s](./Church_of_Sweden \"Church of Sweden\") each [diocese](./Diocese \"Diocese\"). Jämtland is a part of the [Härnösand diocese](./Diocese_of_Härnösand \"Diocese of Härnösand\"), established two years after Jämtland was ceded to Sweden. In Jämtland there are five contracts; [Bräcke-Ragunda](./Bräcke-Ragunda_contract?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Bräcke-Ragunda contract\"), [Krokom-Åre](./Krokom-Åre_contract?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Krokom-Åre contract\"), [Strömsund](./Strömsund\\'s_contract?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Strömsund\\'s contract\") and [Östersund\\'s contract](./Östersund\\'s_contract?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Östersund\\'s contract\"), along with [Berg-Härjedalen](./Berg-Härjedalen\\'s_contract?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Berg-Härjedalen\\'s contract\"). Although only half of the parishes in the last one are actually located in Jämtland, the rest are located in Härjedalen.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Froso_kyrka_side.jpg/250px-Froso_kyrka_side.jpg)](./File:Froso_kyrka_side.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Frösö church](./Frösö_church?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Frösö church\") is located on top of an older Norse cult site.\\n\\nWhen the first churches were established in Jämtland during the medieval period they were done so by a small number of farmers. Estimations show that there were seldom more than 30 to 40 farmers in each parish. In some cases, like in [Kyrkås](./Kyrkås_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Kyrkås parish\"), [Marby](./Marby_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Marby parish\") and [Norderö parish](./Norderö_parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Norderö parish\") the farmers were probably 20 or less. These original parishioners built churches that\\'s lasted for centuries, many are still existing and functioning today. This is quite remarkable given that they built these churches in stones, much larger than their ordinary timber houses and in a material the parishioners were not accustomed to (given that they only used timber). The churches became a matter of concern for every parishioner, the centre in each parish. Everybody had to help build them and their descendants had to maintain them, this carried on for generations. Families have decorated the churches throughout history with various ornaments and art such as valuable inventories, [wood carvings](./Wood_carving \"Wood carving\"), [paintings](./Painting \"Painting\") (predominantly biblical illustrations), [textiles](./Textile \"Textile\"), [silver](./Silver \"Silver\") and [tin](./Tin \"Tin\") along with various [handicrafts](./Handicraft \"Handicraft\"). Almost the entire older [popular culture](./Popular_culture \"Popular culture\") in Jämtland is tied to the churches. Making them the core of Jämtland\\'s cultural heritage.[[15]](./Jämtland#cite_note-15)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Br%C3%A4cke_kyrka.jpg/250px-Br%C3%A4cke_kyrka.jpg)](./File:Bräcke_kyrka.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Neoclassical](./Neoclassicism \"Neoclassicism\") and [Gothic](./Gothic_Revival_architecture \"Gothic Revival architecture\")-styled church in [Bräcke](./Bräcke \"Bräcke\"), built by the parishioners in the 19th century.\\n\\nThe churches have symbolized a connection between Jämtland\\'s population through generations and this is still the case for many today. People are joined through cheerful moments such as [christening](./Baptism \"Baptism\"), [Holy Matrimony](./Marriage \"Marriage\"), [confirmation](./Confirmation#Lutheran_view \"Confirmation\"), through [crisis](./Crisis \"Crisis\") and mournful times like [funerals](./Funeral \"Funeral\"). In Jämtland-Härjedalen the [free church](./Free_church \"Free church\") movement did not become near as widespread as in the rest of Sweden. Because of this Jämtland and Härjedalen have a large number of members in the Swedish church since nine out of ten in fact are members. Although nowadays church attendance is much lower, back then every parishioner gathered on the Sabbath because no one was allowed to work. Within each parish distinctive customs, [bunads](./Bunad \"Bunad\") and dialects developed because of this, especially the dialects are known to differ from parish to parish in Jämtland.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Str%C3%B6msunds_hembygdsg%C3%A5rd3.jpg/330px-Str%C3%B6msunds_hembygdsg%C3%A5rd3.jpg)](./File:Strömsunds_hembygdsgård3.jpg)\\n\\nOld parish house from the 18th century in Ström\\'s parish\\n\\nJämtland also had a great deal of [equality](./Social_equality \"Social equality\") between each parishioner, Jämtland lacked a [nobility](./Nobility \"Nobility\") and there are no noble family coats of arms nor authorial marks in the churches, which is very common in the rest of Sweden. Jämtland also lacked a specific \"bench order\" (an order based on rank that defined where you were allowed to sit in the church), something that other churches had. In Jämtland the principle \"among farmers no other rank except age and life-time\"[[16]](./Jämtland#cite_note-16) applied.\\n\\nEach parish also had an assembly, where every parishioner was present and decisions were only taken unanimously. If they were not able to come to a mutual understanding the matter had to rest and be resumed later until everybody agreed. In the community houses the village\\'s prominent people, so called *byalag*, gathered to decide on mutual concerns such as [split-rail fences](./Split-rail_fence \"Split-rail fence\"), [ditch](./Ditch \"Ditch\") construction and agricultural related stuff. The central figure in each district was the [priest](./Priest \"Priest\"). He dealt with most matters since he was in contact with every parishioner. He meddled in conflicts and gave advice and comfort in various situations. Besides preaching and informing the priest was also a farmer himself, often a forerunner in the field. The priest did not always go the authority\\'s errand, sometimes he tried to help his fellow parishioners fend off extra taxes and military Sami [goahti](./Goahti \"Goahti\") in [Arådalen](./Arådalen \"Arådalen\").\\n\\nIn Jämtland there are also Sami people. The Sami in Jämtland are Southern Sami people and speak [Southern Sami](./Southern_Sami_language \"Southern Sami language\") (or *åarjelsaemien giele*, as it is known in Southern Sami), a [language](./Sami_language \"Sami language\") mutually unintelligible with the other Sami languages. The Sami in Jämtland have historically been referred to as \"Lapps\" and sometimes by using the vague word \"Finns\" (supposedly related to English \"find\", see [Fenni](./Fenni \"Fenni\")), though they prefer to call themselves Sami. There have been Sami peoples in Jämtland from pre-historic times; exactly how many, however, is disputed.[[18]](./Jämtland#cite_note-18) The northernmost part of Jämtland, [Frostviken](./Frostviken_Parish?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Frostviken Parish\"), is originally a Sami area, historically referred to as a *finnmark*. However, the ancestors to the Sami people who live south of this area today probably did not come to the area before the 16th century,[[19]](./Jämtland#cite_note-nationalencyklopedin-19) when large-scale [reindeer](./Reindeer \"Reindeer\") herding began, leading to a nomadic lifestyle among the Sami people. This also led to several conflicts in court between Sami people in Jämtland and the [land owners](./Property \"Property\"). At the dawn of the 20th century, the Swedish state had an official policy which stated that \"Lapp should be Lapp\" and that they should all live a \"traditional\" Sami life and not integrate in the society. This has now changed and only a minority are in fact reindeer-herders. The Sami people in Jämtland are closely connected to their brethren living in Trøndelag, and a distinctive feature of the Southern Sami culture is the [yoik](./Yoik \"Yoik\") called *vuoille*.\\n\\nHeraldry\\n--------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/J%C3%A4mtland_coat_of_arms.png/250px-J%C3%A4mtland_coat_of_arms.png)](./File:Jämtland_coat_of_arms.png)\\n\\nPopular belief holds that the scene represents Jämtland torn between Norway and Sweden.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)\\n\\nThe arms are represented with a ducal coronet. [Blazon](./Blazon \"Blazon\"):\\n\\n:   *I blått fält en gående älg av silver med en lyftande falk på ryggen och i posten åtföljd av en vänstervänd, upprest hund, båda av guld.*[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)[[21]](./Jämtland#cite_note-SHS-21)\\n\\n[English](./English_language \"English language\") translation:\\n\\n:   \"In a blue field, a walking [moose](./Moose \"Moose\") of silver [with red antlers] with a striking falcon on its back accompanied by a reared hound in front, both of gold.\"\\n\\nThe coat of arms of Jämtland, created for [Karl X Gustav](./Charles_X_Gustav_of_Sweden \"Charles X Gustav of Sweden\")\\'s funeral, derived from a seal which had been granted to Jämtland in 1635 by the [Danish-Norwegian king](./Christian_IV_of_Denmark \"Christian IV of Denmark\").[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) The beasts on this seal were difficult to identify. (Is the primary animal a deer, moose or reindeer? Is it a dog, wolf or bear? An eagle or a falcon?) The identity of these animals as a moose between a dog and a falcon was settled in 1884. According to popular perception, these represent Jämtland torn between Norway and Sweden, though obviously this meaning was not officially assigned by any royal authority.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) Svante Höglin claimed the scene to portray a moose hunted by a trained hunting dog and falcon, and in 1935 the coat of arms was revised, adding a collar and a bell to aid in identifying the dog and the falcon, respectively.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20) Strangely, the revised blazon does not mention the moose\\'s [attire](./Antler \"Antler\") although the prototype in the *Riksheraldikerämbetet* (Swedish National Heraldry Office) is provided with secondary colours for the antlers, beak, hooves and claws.[[20]](./Jämtland#cite_note-Nev-20)\\n\\nJämtland\\'s first seal was the one depicted above from the medieval period. It was abolished after the [Nordic Seven Years\\' War](./Nordic_Seven_Years\\'_War \"Nordic Seven Years\\' War\") and the second seal of Jämtland was used between 1575 and 1614. This seal contained two [Olav-axes](./Olav-axe?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Olav-axe\") and was also abolished after a Swedish occupation, the one during the [Kalmar War](./Kalmar_War \"Kalmar War\"). When Jämtland became Swedish it was not suitable to use one of the older seals with such a strong Norwegian influence as a basis for a new Swedish coat of arms. So the latest seal was used instead, even though it was in fact of Danish origin.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*]\\n\\n* [![Arms of the Jämtland Air Force Wing](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/J%C3%A4mtlands_flygflottilj_vapen%2C_pre_1994.svg/120px-J%C3%A4mtlands_flygflottilj_vapen%2C_pre_1994.svg.png)](./File:Jämtlands_flygflottilj_vapen,_pre_1994.svg \"Arms of the Jämtland Air Force Wing\")\\n\\n  Arms of the Jämtland Air Force Wing\\n* [![Arms of Jämtland County](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/J%C3%A4mtland_l%C3%A4n_vapen.svg/120px-J%C3%A4mtland_l%C3%A4n_vapen.svg.png)](./File:Jämtland_län_vapen.svg \"Arms of Jämtland County\")\\n\\n  Arms of Jämtland County\\n\\nCurrent administration\\n----------------------\\n\\nJust like every other historical province of Sweden Jämtland serves no administrative purposes, but serves as an historical, geographical and cultural region. Jämtland makes up three quarters of the [Swedish administrative province](./Län \"Län\") [Jämtland County](./Jämtland_County \"Jämtland County\"), though a small uninhabited part in northern Jämtland is a part of [Västerbotten County](./Västerbotten_County \"Västerbotten County\") and the area around [Överturingen](./Överturingen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Överturingen\") is a part of [Västernorrland County](./Västernorrland_County \"Västernorrland County\"). The landsting, *[County Council](./County_Councils_of_Sweden \"County Councils of Sweden\")*, is an elected assembly and the successor of Jamtamót. This County Council was the role model for the rest of the Swedish County Councils when they were established in 1863.[[22]](./Jämtland#cite_note-22)\\n\\nThe province is also divided into primarily seven [municipalities](./Municipalities \"Municipalities\"); [Berg Municipality](./Berg_Municipality \"Berg Municipality\"), [Bräcke Municipality](./Bräcke_Municipality \"Bräcke Municipality\"), [Krokom Municipality](./Krokom_Municipality \"Krokom Municipality\"), [Ragunda Municipality](./Ragunda_Municipality \"Ragunda Municipality\"), [Strömsund Municipality](./Strömsund_Municipality \"Strömsund Municipality\"), [Åre Municipality](./Åre_Municipality \"Åre Municipality\") and [Östersund Municipality](./Östersund_Municipality \"Östersund Municipality\"). The uninhabited part in northern Jämtland belongs to [Dorotea Municipality](./Dorotea_Municipality \"Dorotea Municipality\") and the area around Överturingen is a part of [Ånge Municipality](./Ånge_Municipality \"Ånge Municipality\").\\n\\nThough, even if these municipalities and the county are serving as administrative regions most Jamts still identify themselves with the parishes and with Jämtland as a province.\\n\\nPhysical geography\\n------------------\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| [icon](./File:Question_book-new.svg) | This section **does not [cite](./Wikipedia:Citing_sources \"Wikipedia:Citing sources\") any [sources](./Wikipedia:Verifiability \"Wikipedia:Verifiability\")**. Please help [improve this section](./Special:EditPage/Jämtland \"Special:EditPage/Jämtland\") by [adding citations to reliable sources](./Help:Referencing_for_beginners \"Help:Referencing for beginners\"). Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](./Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence \"Wikipedia:Verifiability\"). *(December 2024)* *([Learn how and when to remove this message](./Help:Maintenance_template_removal \"Help:Maintenance template removal\"))* |\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Storsj%C3%B6n_med_fj%C3%A4ll.jpg/250px-Storsj%C3%B6n_med_fj%C3%A4ll.jpg)](./File:Storsjön_med_fjäll.jpg)\\n\\nThe mountains in Scandinavia are referred to as *[fells](./Fell \"Fell\")*. This picture shows Storsjön, \"the Great Lake\" and distant fells.\\n\\nJämtland is a large land-locked province in the heart of the [Scandinavian Peninsula](./Scandinavian_Peninsula \"Scandinavian Peninsula\") in [northern Europe](./Northern_Europe \"Northern Europe\"). Jämtland stretches 315 kilometers in north–south direction and 250 kilometers in east–west direction and is equal in size with e.g. [Ireland](./Ireland \"Ireland\"). Jämtland\\'s western border is made out by [Kölen](./Scandinavian_Mountains \"Scandinavian Mountains\") which stretches throughout the province from north to south with branches into the landscape\\'s southeastern parts. The fell [massif](./Massif \"Massif\") is broken at some places by large valleys stretching all the way to the [Norwegian Sea](./Norwegian_Sea \"Norwegian Sea\"). These valleys have been used for centuries as paths connecting Jämtland to the west. The valleys were particularly heavily used during [pilgrimages](./Pilgrimage \"Pilgrimage\") to [Nidaros](./Nidaros \"Nidaros\"), the fourth most visited pilgrimage site during the medieval period. In fact no less than three pilgrim roads went through Jämtland.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/T%C3%A4nnforsen.jpg/250px-T%C3%A4nnforsen.jpg)](./File:Tännforsen.jpg)\\n\\n[Tännforsen](./Tännforsen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Tännforsen\") in western Jämtland\\n\\nThe entire province is more or less a [highland region](./Highland_(geography) \"Highland (geography)\") with the highest peak being [Storsylen](./Storsylen \"Storsylen\"), a peak in the [Sylan](./Sylan \"Sylan\") mountain range with an [altitude](./Altitude \"Altitude\") of 1 728 meters above sea level. Though this is not the highest peak in the mountain range, since that peak is in fact located on the other side of the border. Another large peak in Jämtland worthy of mention is [Åreskutan](./Åreskutan \"Åreskutan\") (1 420 meters above sea level).\\nThe lowest point in the province is as low as 35 meters above sea level and is located in the eastern part of Jämtland.\\n\\nApproximately 8 per cent of Jämtland\\'s area is covered by water and the province has two larger [streams](./Stream \"Stream\"), [Ljungan](./Ljungan \"Ljungan\") and [Indalsälven](./Indalsälven \"Indalsälven\") (also known as *Jämtlandsälven*). Both of which emanates from the Scandinavian Mountains and drains several lakes on their way eastwards to lower altitudes.\\n\\n### Climate\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Jamtlandvy.jpg/250px-Jamtlandvy.jpg)](./File:Jamtlandvy.jpg)\\n\\nSummer scenery in Jämtland\\n\\nJämtland has a [temperate climate](./Temperate_climate \"Temperate climate\") and belongs to the [temperate zone](./Temperate_zone \"Temperate zone\")\\'s northernmost area. The climate in Jämtland is both [humid continental](./Humid_continental_climate \"Humid continental climate\") and [subarctic](./Subarctic_climate \"Subarctic climate\"), depending on the location. The climate is greatly affected by the [Norwegian Sea](./Norwegian_Sea \"Norwegian Sea\") and the [Atlantic Ocean](./Atlantic_Ocean \"Atlantic Ocean\"), due to several [mountain passes](./Mountain_pass \"Mountain pass\") in Scandinavian mountain range.\\n\\nIn western Jämtland mild winters with excessive [precipitation](./Precipitation_(meteorology) \"Precipitation (meteorology)\") are common. This is because of the warm winds brought to the area by the [Gulf Stream](./Gulf_Stream \"Gulf Stream\"). The average precipitation in the Jamtish Fells is roughly 1 000 [millimetres](./Millimetre \"Millimetre\") per year, with [Skäckerfjällen](./Skäckerfjällen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Skäckerfjällen\") as extreme with about 1 500\\xa0mm. The precipitation rates in the middle of the province are much more moderate. In fact the central and eastern parts of Jämtland have precipitation shortages, in Storsjöbygden the annual averages is as low as 500\\xa0mm. Due to the warm winds the temperature during the winters reaches its maximum in the fell region with about -7-8[°C](./°C \"°C\") in [Storlien](./Storlien \"Storlien\") and the environs. The coldest winter temperatures are found in the province\\'s outskirts like [Börtnan](./Börtnan?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Börtnan\") with roughly -11\\xa0°C.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Maximum temperatures in the summer months average from the 14\\xa0°C in Jämtland\\'s eastern parts to around 11\\xa0°C in the fell region.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] Though on certain mountain peaks the averages are usually as low as 5\\xa0°C.\\n\\nThe highest (34.0\\xa0°C) and lowest (-45.8\\xa0°C) temperatures ever recorded in Jämtland were found in its easternmost parts near [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand \"Hammarstrand\") in 1947 and 1950, respectively.\\n\\n[Blizzards](./Blizzard \"Blizzard\") are common in Jämtland, and especially in the fell region. The most notable blizzard is the one that arose on [New Year\\'s Eve](./New_Year\\'s_Eve \"New Year\\'s Eve\") 1718 (see above). The heaviest winds in Jämtland may gust to 55 metres/s (198\\xa0km/h, 123\\xa0mph).\\n\\nWildlife\\n--------\\n\\n### Flora\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG/120px-Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG)](./File:Nigritella_nigra_brunkulla.JPG)\\n\\n*Gymnadenia nigra*, known as *brunkulla* — the *brown maiden* in Jamtish dialect.\\n\\nThe Jamtish [flora](./Flora \"Flora\") is heavily characterized by [temperate coniferous forest](./Temperate_coniferous_forest \"Temperate coniferous forest\"), [taiga](./Taiga \"Taiga\"), a forest inhabited by [Norway spruce](./Norway_spruce \"Norway spruce\") and [pine](./Pine \"Pine\") trees. Among the two the Norway spruce is more common. The Norway spruce actually grows most densely in Jämtland together with the southern parts of [Lapland](./Lapland,_Sweden \"Lapland, Sweden\"). Here roughly 60 percent of the forests consist of spruces.\\n\\nIn Jämtland over 2,300 mineral-rich [marshes](./Marsh \"Marsh\") ([wetlands](./Wetland \"Wetland\")) containing a very high [pH](./PH \"PH\") level have been located. These marshes cover an area of 550 square kilometers. 400 of these marshes are also very rich in [chalk](./Chalk \"Chalk\") and because of the chalk-rich soil Jämtland displays the largest concentration of these types of marshes on the entire European continent. The chalk-rich soil has attracted several chalk-dependent plants, such as [orchids](./Orchid \"Orchid\"), in Jämtland there are 19 different kinds of orchids.\\n\\nEach province in Sweden has symbols associated with them and Jämtland\\'s provincial [flower](./Flower \"Flower\") is an extremely rare orchid, the *[Gymnadenia nigra](./Gymnadenia_nigra \"Gymnadenia nigra\")*, an orchid that\\'s only common in the province and a few other places in central Scandinavia. Several kinds of [berries](./Berry \"Berry\") are found in Jämtland like e.g. [bilberry](./Bilberry \"Bilberry\") (*blåbär*), [lingonberry](./Lingonberry \"Lingonberry\") (*lyngbär*) and [cloudberry](./Cloudberry \"Cloudberry\") (referred to as *mylhta* in Jämtland).\\n\\n### Fauna\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg/250px-Moose_Zoo_%C3%96stersund.jpg)](./File:Moose_Zoo_Östersund.jpg)\\n\\nA tame Jamtish moose from [Moose Garden](./Moose_Garden?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Moose Garden\") in [Orrviken](./Orrviken \"Orrviken\") outside Östersund. The moose is Jämtland\\'s provincial animal.\\n\\nDue to the diversified [natural environment](./Natural_environment \"Natural environment\") in Jämtland it displays a great deal of different [animals](./Animal \"Animal\"). The animal most commonly associated with Jämtland is (as already hinted) the [moose](./Moose \"Moose\"). It is Jämtland\\'s provincial animal and is referred to in dialect as simply *djur*, \"animal\". Moose may be found throughout Jämtland but to a lesser extent in the mountainous area in the province\\'s eastern parts and in the north.\\n\\nHowever northern Jämtland is the most densely populated [brown bear](./Brown_bear \"Brown bear\") habitat in the world. The brown bear (*bjenn* in Jamtish) is also more or less common throughout Jämtland. Other large predators in Jämtland include the [cat](./Felidae \"Felidae\") *gaupa* ([Eurasian lynx](./Eurasian_lynx \"Eurasian lynx\")), the *filfras* meaning the glutton ([wolverine](./Wolverine \"Wolverine\")) and smaller such as the [Arctic fox](./Arctic_fox \"Arctic fox\"). Jämtland has had populations of [wolves](./Wolf \"Wolf\") (*skrågg*, *gråbein*) from time to time after it practically became extinct in Scandinavia during the 20th century. There are however currently no wolves with an established [territory](./Territory_(animal) \"Territory (animal)\") in Jämtland. There is also one large [raptor](./Bird_of_prey \"Bird of prey\") in the province, the [golden eagle](./Golden_eagle \"Golden eagle\").\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Beaver_dam_J%C3%A4mtland.JPG/250px-Beaver_dam_J%C3%A4mtland.JPG)](./File:Beaver_dam_Jämtland.JPG)\\n\\nA [beaver dam](./Beaver_dam \"Beaver dam\") in Jämtland.\\n\\nThe last native [beaver](./Beaver \"Beaver\") in Sweden was shot in northern Jämtland 1871 at [Bjurälven](./Bjurälven \"Bjurälven\") (*bjur* or *björ* is the Jamtish word for beaver). It was also in Jämtland that the beaver was reintroduced in Sweden from Norway in 1922. The current beaver population is quite large and common. Among the smaller mammals inhabiting Jämtland that are rare in the rest of Scandinavia are e.g. the [taiga shrew](./Taiga_shrew \"Taiga shrew\") and the [northern birch mouse](./Northern_birch_mouse \"Northern birch mouse\"). The *læmel*, [Norway lemming](./Norway_lemming \"Norway lemming\") is also present in Jämtland and the latest major population boom usual for this species occurred in 2001.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Albino_raindeer.jpg/250px-Albino_raindeer.jpg)](./File:Albino_raindeer.jpg)\\n\\nReindeer in Jämtland\\'s mountain range.\\n\\nJämtland is inhabited by several mammals from the [weasel family](./Weasel_family \"Weasel family\"). Besides the already mentioned wolverine the *oter*, [otter](./Eurasian_otter \"Eurasian otter\"), is widespread in the province and common near several streams, the [least or snow weasel](./Least_weasel \"Least weasel\") exists, along with planted, released and escaped [minks](./Mink \"Mink\"). The province is also home to the [pine marten](./Pine_marten \"Pine marten\") and the [ermine](./Stoat \"Stoat\"). These mammals have often been hunted for their valuable fur, for Jämtland this is especially true for the ermine.\\n\\nAmong the [deer](./Deer \"Deer\") the moose is as already stated common. Other deer are [roe deer](./Roe_deer \"Roe deer\"), [red deer](./Red_deer \"Red deer\") and [reindeer](./Reindeer \"Reindeer\"), in the shape of Sami herds or wilded originally tame reindeers.\\n\\nThe provincial [fish](./Fish \"Fish\") is the [brown trout](./Brown_trout \"Brown trout\") which is found together with [common whitefish](./Common_whitefish \"Common whitefish\"), [grayling](./Thymallus_thymallus \"Thymallus thymallus\"), [European perch](./European_perch \"European perch\"), [Arctic char](./Arctic_char \"Arctic char\"), [burbot](./Burbot \"Burbot\"), [salmon](./Salmon \"Salmon\") and the carnivorous [northern pike](./Northern_pike \"Northern pike\"). Roughly 250 types of [birds](./Bird \"Bird\") have been observed in Jämtland. The species presence greatly varies, in the fells [bluethroat](./Bluethroat \"Bluethroat\"), [long-tailed skua](./Long-tailed_skua \"Long-tailed skua\"), [Eurasian dotterel](./Eurasian_dotterel \"Eurasian dotterel\"), [ptarmigan](./Rock_ptarmigan \"Rock ptarmigan\"), [Lapland](./Lapland_bunting \"Lapland bunting\") and [snow bunting](./Snow_bunting \"Snow bunting\") are found. The forested region is inhabited by species such as [hazel hen](./Hazel_hen \"Hazel hen\"), [black grouse](./Black_grouse \"Black grouse\"), [capercaillie](./Capercaillie \"Capercaillie\"), [Siberian jay](./Siberian_jay \"Siberian jay\"), [three-toed woodpecker](./Eurasian_three-toed_woodpecker \"Eurasian three-toed woodpecker\") and [rustic bunting](./Rustic_bunting \"Rustic bunting\"). Several different types of [owls](./Owl \"Owl\") dwells in the province and the provincial owl is the [northern hawk owl](./Northern_hawk_owl \"Northern hawk owl\").\\n\\nEconomy\\n-------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg/250px-Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg)](./File:Jon_Olsson_invitational.jpg)\\n\\nThe [freeskiing](./Freeskiing \"Freeskiing\") competition [Jon Olsson](./Jon_Olsson \"Jon Olsson\") invitational in [Åre](./Åre \"Åre\")\\n\\nThe first humans came to Jämtland after the last ice age and later switched to a more agricultural lifestyle. Though the agriculture could not sustain the population so it was combined with a great deal of trading, hunting and iron production. When the rise of industrialism begun, Jämtland was one of the few Swedish regions that never became fully industrialized. Instead Jämtland supplied the Norrlandic coast with raw materials, mainly [lumber](./Lumber \"Lumber\"). The focus in Jämtland\\'s [economy](./Economy \"Economy\") was directed towards tourism after the construction of the railroad, starting with the \"clean air tourists\" who came to experience the fresh air, to see the snow clad fells, the waterfalls and the natural environment. Today the tourism in Jämtland is dominated by winter sports and especially alpine skiing in various facilities in [Åre](./Åre_(ski_area) \"Åre (ski area)\"), [Bydalen](./Bydalen?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Bydalen\"), [Storlien](./Storlien \"Storlien\"), [Klövsjö](./Klövsjö \"Klövsjö\"), etc.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Lill%C3%A4nge_handelsplats_070616.jpg/250px-Lill%C3%A4nge_handelsplats_070616.jpg)](./File:Lillänge_handelsplats_070616.jpg)\\n\\n[Lillänge](./Lillänge?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Lillänge\") is an external shopping centre in Östersund\\n\\nAs Jämtland never industrialized the agricultural sector is larger compared to the rest of Sweden. In Jämtland County this sector employs 4,4 per cent of the labour force compared to 1,8 per cent for Sweden as whole.[[23]](./Jämtland#cite_note-23) Just like the rest of Sweden the [public sector](./Public_sector \"Public sector\") in Jämtland is large and the high [taxes](./Taxes \"Taxes\") fund the [public welfare](./Swedish_welfare \"Swedish welfare\").\\n\\nJämtland has large concentrations of [uranium](./Uranium \"Uranium\") and deposits of e.g. [gold](./Gold \"Gold\"), [zinc](./Zinc \"Zinc\"), [mica](./Mica \"Mica\"), [silver](./Silver \"Silver\"), [lead](./Lead \"Lead\"), [iron](./Iron \"Iron\") and [copper](./Copper \"Copper\") have been found. However, the only [mines](./Mining \"Mining\") of importance in Jämtland\\'s history are the former copper mines in [Fröå](./Fröå?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Fröå\") and [Huså](./Huså?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Huså\").\\n\\nJämtland is heavily dominated by many [small businesses](./Small_business \"Small business\") and together with Härjedalen Jämtland has the second highest number of [company owners](./Company_owner \"Company owner\") in Sweden (in relation to the population), the highest number of enterprising women[[24]](./Jämtland#cite_note-24) and by far the most [cooperatives](./Cooperative \"Cooperative\").[[25]](./Jämtland#cite_note-25) [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\") is the centre of trade and commerce in Jämtland.\\n\\nPopulation\\n----------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg/250px-20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg)](./File:20080719ChulalongkornPavilionIMG_6672.jpg)\\n\\n[King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building](./King_Chulalongkorn_Memorial_Building \"King Chulalongkorn Memorial Building\") nearby the small village [Bispgården](./Västra_Bispgården \"Västra Bispgården\"), easternmost Jämtland\\n\\nWith the exception of the city of [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\") and its surrounding areas, Jämtland is a very sparsely populated region. In Jämtland as a whole, there are only 3.4 people per square kilometre, and the population of 115,331[[1]](./Jämtland#cite_note-population-1) is unevenly distributed, with more than half its population (approximately 60\\xa0000) living in the Östersund area.\\n\\nIn Jämtland County (including the province of Härjedalen) the number of people living outside an urban area is 34% of the total population, making Jämtland one of the largest rural regions in Scandinavia. Most people in Jämtland live in [Storsjöbygden](./Storsjöbygden?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Storsjöbygden\"), the area around lake Storsjön which includes Jämtland\\'s only [chartered city](./Cities_of_Sweden \"Cities of Sweden\"), [Östersund](./Östersund \"Östersund\"), founded 1786 (now including Frösön), [Krokom](./Krokom \"Krokom\"), [Ås](./Ås,_Krokom \"Ås, Krokom\"), [Svenstavik](./Svenstavik \"Svenstavik\"), [Nälden](./Nälden \"Nälden\") and Jämtland\\'s second largest town [Brunflo](./Brunflo \"Brunflo\"). This region is actually quite densely populated. The largest urban areas outside Storsjöbygden are primly the municipality seats [Strömsund](./Strömsund \"Strömsund\"), [Järpen](./Järpen \"Järpen\"), [Bräcke](./Bräcke \"Bräcke\") and [Hammarstrand](./Hammarstrand \"Hammarstrand\"), along with towns such as [Hammerdal](./Hammerdal \"Hammerdal\"), Lit, and the ski resort [Åre](./Åre \"Åre\").\\n\\nA resident or native of Jämtland is commonly referred to as *Jamt* (Swedish: *jämte*).\\n\\n### Famous natives\\n\\n* [Kjell Albin Abrahamson](./Kjell_Albin_Abrahamson \"Kjell Albin Abrahamson\"), journalist and author\\n* [Georg
